round11_research.bug_semantics: The JavaScript Code node executes user code in the task-runner Node VM with host objects injected into the sandbox. `$input.constructor.constructor.prototype` is the host Function.prototype. The freeze loop only froze prototypes with `typeof === 'object'`, but `typeof Function.prototype === 'function'`, so that prototype stayed mutable. An authenticated user who can create and execute workflows can pollute Function.prototype, recover host globalThis, and complete a sandbox escape when allowlisted imports (NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_BUILTIN / NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_EXTERNAL) supply gadgets. CWE-1321. Patched in 1.123.69, 2.33.4, and 2.34.1 by freezing function-typed prototypes as well (`isFreezable` = object or function).

round11_research.bug_semantics: PluginImportGuard is a sys.meta_path hook plus a sys.modules hider that is supposed to block dangerous imports at plugin runtime. Its denylist is CWE-184-incomplete: ALWAYS_BLOCKED is only {ctypes, __builtin__, __builtins__} and CAPABILITY_GATED adds subprocess (always), os (always), and socket (NETWORK_ACCESS). _should_block_module() returns False for every other top-level name, so find_module()/find_spec() do not raise and hide_dangerous_modules() never removes those names from sys.modules. After 50bec5d the AST analyzer's DANGEROUS_MODULES independently treats sys, shutil, multiprocessing, importlib, pickle, shelve, pty, fcntl, pwd, grp, signal, resource, pipes, popen2, and platform as never-importable; an attacker who bypasses that static pass (string obfuscation, encoding, or __import__ indirection) can therefore import those modules at runtime and reach arbitrary code execution (pickle.__reduce__, importlib, sys.modules, shutil, multiprocessing). Direct `import pickle`/`import sys` is the sink; AST is only the bypassable outer check.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-74886 state=PUBLISHED (not rejected/withdrawn); CNA VulnCheck; affected openssl_encrypt >=0 <1.4.0, 1.4.0 unaffected; CWE-184; GHSA-c7vw-vfxj-3mvh withdrawn_at=null. round11_research.bug_semantics: Snowflake executeQuery builds sqlText from the Query parameter after n8n expression resolution and calls snowflake-sdk execute with empty binds. A workflow that embeds untrusted item/webhook data in that query (historically via getNodeParameter expression evaluation; after the SQL-editor overhaul via getResolvables + evaluateExpression string-replace) interpolates attacker-controlled bytes into the SQL command. Insert/Update already used positional ? binds; executeQuery did not, so quotes/operators in expression values become SQL syntax (CWE-89). Exploitation requires a workflow author to place externally controlled expressions in the raw query.

round11_research.bug_semantics: MCP create_workflow_from_code persists node.credentials after validateWorkflowCredentialReferences. That validator's computeActiveCredentialTypes copies the runtime CredentialsPermissionChecker.getActiveCredentialTypes filter: it inserts the unresolved string values of node.parameters.nodeCredentialType and genericAuthType into the active-type set, then skips any credential key not in that set. When the authentication type is an n8n expression (for example `={{ "httpHeaderAuth" }}`), the raw expression never equals the real credential key, so the project-scope ownership classifier is skipped and a credential ID from another project is written onto the new workflow. Exploitation needs MCP enabled, a valid MCP Bearer API key, and knowledge of a target credential ID. The execution-time permission gate still refuses to load the foreign credential, so the impact is unauthorized persistence of a cross-project credential reference (CWE-639), not secret exfiltration.

round11_research.bug_semantics: IndexFile.remove() and Head.checkout() forward caller **kwargs into `git rm` and `git checkout` with no allow_unsafe_options/check_unsafe_options gate. GitPython's transform_kwargs/dashify turns pathspec_from_file=<path> and pathspec_file_nul=True into --pathspec-from-file=<path> --pathspec-file-nul, placed before any `--` pathspec separator. Git then treats the named file as one NUL-delimited pathspec and quotes the entire unmatched pathspec in its error; GitPython returns that text on GitCommandError.stderr, disclosing any process-readable file whose contents do not match a tracked path. Same primitive as TagReference.create() -F in GHSA-3f7w-8rr8-f37f, at two sites that advisory's sweep assessed as non-disclosing.

round11_research.bug_semantics: GitPython clone APIs (Repo.clone, Repo.clone_from, and submodule clone) forward caller-controlled git-clone options after checking them against Repo.unsafe_git_clone_options. Through 3.1.53 that denylist was only --upload-pack/-u and --config/-c, omitting --template. Under the default allow_unsafe_options=False, Git._option_candidates turns template='<dir>' into --template and check_unsafe_options lets it through; git clone --template=<dir> then copies <dir>/hooks into the new repository and runs post-checkout during checkout, yielding arbitrary command execution. Independent of short-option value-smuggling; --template is a legitimate long option. CWE-184/CWE-78.

round11_research.bug_semantics: GitPython's config writer interpolates option names verbatim into git-config lines (`write_section` emits `\t%s = %s\n`). Through 3.1.57, `_assure_config_name_safe(option, "option")` rejected only CR/LF/NUL, so `=`, `#`, `;`, brackets, and whitespace in an option name were accepted. A caller-controlled name such as `sshCommand = touch /tmp/RCE #` is written as `\tsshCommand = touch /tmp/RCE # = <value>`, which git parses as `core.sshCommand=touch /tmp/RCE` (the `#` comments out the intended value). That forges `core.sshCommand` / `core.hooksPath` / `alias.*` and yields RCE on a later git operation. Distinct field and character class from section-header bracket injection and from newline injection.

round11_research.bug_semantics: GitPython's IndexFile.checkout() and TagReference.create() each accept **kwargs and forward them, unguarded, into git checkout-index and git tag. Git.cmd.transform_kwargs turns prefix=<path> into --prefix=<path> (checkout-index prepends that path to every blob it writes, including absolute destinations and -f overwrites) and F=<file>/file=<file> into -F/--file (git tag stores the file bytes as the annotated tag message, which GitPython returns in-band via TagReference.tag.message). Neither call site had allow_unsafe_options nor Git.check_unsafe_options, so caller-influenced kwargs were a direct filesystem write/read primitive. CVE-2026-73620 / vendor GHSA-3f7w-8rr8-f37f; affected < 3.1.57; CVSS 8.1 (overwrite). A later positional TagReference.create bypass of the kwargs-only guard is a different advisory (GHSA-3wxw-xv34-2frg), not this case.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Ech0 access tokens created with expiry=never (NEVER_EXPIRY, duration 0) are signed as JWTs with no exp claim. jwt/v5 and JWTAuthMiddleware accept that token, so a stolen bearer stays cryptographically valid until JWT_SECRET rotation. Three independent revocation paths then fail for this token class: AuthHandler.Logout dereferences claims.ExpiresAt.Time and panics on the nil field so the JTI never reaches the blacklist; AuthRepository.RevokeToken returns immediately when remainTTL <= 0; SettingService.DeleteAccessToken deletes only the metadata row and does not blacklist the JTI. Finite-expiry tokens can still age out; never-expire tokens cannot.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Ech0 stored local-account passwords as a single unsalted MD5 hex digest. MD5Encrypt(text) is crypto/md5.New, Write([]byte(text)), Sum(nil), hex.EncodeToString — no salt, no iteration, no memory-hard KDF. Through 5.4.1 every local-password path used that helper: InitOwner and Register persist MD5Encrypt(password) into users.password; Login hashes the submitted password the same way and does a string equality check against the stored digest; UpdateUser rewrites users.password with another unsalted MD5. An attacker who obtains data/ech0.db (backup export, mis-served static files, or filesystem access) can extract the 32-hex hashes and recover owner/admin plaintext with rainbow tables or GPU hashcat -m 0, then POST /api/login for a full session JWT. CWE-327. Fixed in 5.4.2 by moving the secret into user_local_auth, hashing new passwords with bcrypt, and lazily upgrading leftover MD5 rows on next successful login.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Scriban's template builtin array.insert_at (ArrayFunctions.InsertAt) pads the target list by running a tight C# for-loop from list.Count up to an attacker-controlled index and calling Add(null) each step, then Inserts the value. That fill never calls TemplateContext.StepLoop and never consults LoopLimit, LimitToString, RecursiveLimit, or ObjectRecursionLimit, even though LoopLimit (default 1000) existed from the first commit for script for-statements. A one-line template such as {{ [1] | array.insert_at 200000000 'x' | array.size }} therefore allocates unbounded memory, raises OutOfMemoryException, and can terminate the host process in well under a second. The 7.0.0 sibling hardening (dde661d36bb6b06414546c6b1272fc1b517078c9) added StepLoop overloads to other ArrayFunctions primitives and still left InsertAt on the unbounded IEnumerable/int/object signature. round11_research.bug_semantics: Scriban's array multiplication operator (array * integer) in ScriptArray<T>.TryEvaluate allocates a result whose size is the product of an attacker-controlled integer and the source array length. The fill path pre-sizes with unchecked int arithmetic (intModifier * array.Count) and then copies via a C# for-loop of AddRange with no LoopLimit/StepLoop/LimitToString check. A ~40-byte template such as {{ [1,2,3,4,5] * 200000000 }} therefore forces a multi-gigabyte allocation (or an overflow ArgumentOutOfRangeException wrapped as ScriptRuntimeException) instead of the documented iteration limit (default 1000).

round11_research.bug_semantics: Scriban expression evaluation (CWE-400) lets a template author exhaust memory or CPU on three paths that ignore existing LoopLimit/LimitToString controls. Vector 1: ScriptBinaryExpression.CalculateToString implements string*int as an unbounded C# for-loop that Appends into a StringBuilder, so '{{ 'AAAA' * 500000000 }}' attempts a multi-gigabyte allocation even when LimitToString defaults to 1MB. Vector 2: CalculateLongWithInt and CalculateBigIntegerNoFit apply BigInteger << (int)right with no cap, so '{{ 1 << 100000000 }}' allocates an arbitrarily large integer (Power is capped with MaxBigInteger, but shift is not). Vector 3: '..' / '..<' produce lazy RangeInclude/RangeExclude iterators; ArrayFunctions.Size fully enumerates via Cast<object>().Count() and Join appends with no size bound, never calling StepLoop(), so '{{ (0..1000000000) | array.size }}' burns CPU despite LoopLimit=1000. OutOfMemoryException typically terminates the host process. Vendor/CVE range is all versions before 7.0.0.
evidence: CVE record https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-74785 state=PUBLISHED (VulnCheck CNA, datePublic 2026-03-22); not rejected/withdrawn. GHSA-q5qx-vc88-69hw is the unreviewed NVD/GitHub wrapper for that CVE; vendor advisory is GHSA-xw6w-9jjh-p9cr (reviewed, withdrawn_at null, vulnerable < 7.0.0, patched 7.0.0).

round11_research.bug_semantics: Scriban's recursive-descent parser treats nested array initializers as expressions. ParseArrayInitializer consumes '[' then calls ExpectAndParseExpression, which calls ParseExpression; ParseExpression on TokenType.OpenBracket calls ParseArrayInitializer again. Deeply nested input such as '{{ ' + new string('[', 5000) + '1' + new string(']', 5000) + ' }}' therefore grows C# call-stack frames without a terminating depth bound. The GHSA-wgh7-7m3c-fx25 6.6.0 mitigation (default ExpressionDepthLimit applied inside EnterExpression) did not wrap ParseArrayInitializer, and at 6.6.0 EnterExpression only logged once then continued parsing, so Template.Parse of untrusted nested arrays still raised an uncatchable StackOverflowException and killed the process (CWE-674).

round11_research.bug_semantics: Stored XSS in the conversion-table search highlighter. ConvertTable/ConversionTable parses MISP/STIX conversion input_text and output_text into cell strings, then when a search is active renders those cells with Vue v-html="highlight(String(row[col.key]))". highlight() regex-escaped only the query and wrapped matches in <mark class="ctbl-mark"> without HTML-escaping the cell, so markup stored in conversion data (for example a MISP Attribute.value or STIX name/pattern) was interpreted as HTML. The empty-query branch of highlight() returned the raw string, but the template already used escaped [[ ]] interpolation when search was empty; the exploitable sink is the search-active v-html path. CVE-2026-73161 remains PUBLISHED (CIRCL CNA; GHSA withdrawn_at null). Vendor v1.5 notes list this as CWE-79 affecting 1.4; the CNA range 0..1.4.0 is broader than git history because the table view did not exist at v1.3.

round11_research.bug_semantics: python_sandbox_server's RestrictedPython sandbox in server_fastmcp.py is bypassable because create_safe_globals() exposes CPython's raw getattr/setattr (and hasattr) in safe_builtins, execute() never installs a RestrictedPython _getattr_ guard (only _getiter_/_getitem_), and the builtins merge does merged_builtins.update(our_builtins) so the raw getattr overwrites RestrictedPython's controlled entries. validate_code() then only substring-matches literal dunders such as '__class__', which a payload can construct at runtime. An attacker who can call the execute_code MCP tool walks the class hierarchy through getattr, reaches subprocess.Popen, and runs OS commands as the server process. HTTP/SSE exposure without auth (added later) raises this to unauthenticated RCE when that transport is enabled; the getattr hole itself is present from first write.

round11_research.bug_semantics: CWE-416 use-after-free of a function pointer in miSyncDestroyFence(). When a fence is destroyed, the function sets sync.beingDestroyed and walks pFence->sync.pTriglist, invoking each trigger's CounterDestroyed callback (SyncAwaitTriggerFired for Await) before capturing ptl->next and freeing the list node. CounterDestroyed can FreeResource the Await, and FreeAwait then frees the entire SyncAwaitUnion for that Await group while skipping SyncDeleteTriggerFromSyncObject because beingDestroyed is already set. If one Await has multiple conditions on the same fence, later SyncTriggerList nodes still hold pTrigger pointers into the freed union; the next iteration performs (*ptl->pTrigger->CounterDestroyed) on dangling memory. A local client can Await a fence with multiple triggers, then a second connection DestroyFence to crash the server or escalate if it runs as root.

round11_research.bug_semantics: CWE-674 uncontrolled recursion in liquidjs `{% layout %}` / `{% block %}`. In STORE mode, `src/tags/block.ts` `getBlockRender` records a per-name render function in `ctx.getRegister('blocks')[this.block]`. When a child template nests a block inside another block of the same name (including anonymous `{%block%}`), the inner tag looks up that register, wraps the outer render as `renderChild`, and overwrites the slot. OUTPUT-mode layout then calls the inner wrapper; the outer templates still contain the inner same-name block, which looks up the same register and re-enters `renderChild` with no cycle check. Recursion allocates renderer/emitter frames until the Node.js heap OOMs (~4GB). The 2016 layout/block implementation stored rendered HTML strings and could not form this call cycle. GHSA-4rc3-7j7w-m548 / CVE-2026-41311 (NVD Analyzed, not withdrawn) patch the path in `e2311dfd6e82f73509308aa8a3a1fafc92e226f0` by pushing the current Tag onto a `blockStack` register and throwing `block tag cannot be nested`. Advisory range is `< 10.25.7` (first_patched 10.25.7); the fix commit is already an ancestor of tag v10.25.6.

round11_research.bug_semantics: LiquidJS replace_first performs first-occurrence substitution by delegating to JavaScript String.prototype.replace (originally lodash _.replace, which is native String#replace). A string replacement is therefore a JS replacement pattern: $& expands to the entire matched substring, and $` / $' expand similarly. After memoryLimit landed, the filter charged only the input length (later input+args), never the expanded output. An attacker who can supply a Liquid template can chain assign plus replace_first with a replacement of many $& tokens, amplifying a 1-byte string through ~50x stages to hundreds of megabytes while the limiter records only the unamplified inputs, causing heap growth and event-loop DoS. Sibling replace uses split/join (literal $&) and replace_last uses substring, so only replace_first has this expansion path.

round11_research.bug_semantics: LiquidJS documents RenderOptions.ownPropertyOnly as a per-render lockdown that hides prototype-chain properties for a single parseAndRender()/render() call. round11_research.bug_semantics: OliveTin JWT authentication accepts a validly signed token whose aud claim does not match the configured authJwtAud when the token is verified with a local RSA public key (authJwtPubKeyPath) or HMAC secret (authJwtHmacSecret). parseJwtTokenWithLocalKey and parseJwtTokenWithHMAC call github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5 jwt.Parse with only a keyfunc and no jwt.WithAudience option, so golang-jwt never checks audience. The sibling remote JWKS path parseJwtTokenWithRemoteKey does pass jwt.WithAudience(cfg.AuthJwtAud). An attacker who holds a token minted for a different audience/service that shares the signing material can authenticate (WhoAmI and other JWT-gated APIs). ACL authorization is not bypassed; this is authentication-time audience non-enforcement (CWE-287/CWE-345).

round11_research.bug_semantics: OliveTin RestartAction is a confused deputy: it looks up a prior execution by tracking ID, then calls StartAction with a newly constructed connect.Request that carries only BindingId and UniqueTrackingId and does not copy the original caller's Cookie/Authorization headers. StartAction authenticates with auth.UserFromApiCall(ctx, req, cfg), which runs the cookie/header auth chain against that synthetic request. Missing credentials make UserFromApiCall fall back to the guest user, so a low-privilege authenticated caller whose exec permission is false can still cause the bound shell action to run if guest.exec is true.

round11_research.bug_semantics: ProcXFixesSetClientDisconnectMode in xfixes/disconnect.c does a REQUEST() cast of the client request buffer and then copies stuff->disconnect_mode without REQUEST_SIZE_MATCH. A local X11 client can send a shorter-than-struct SetClientDisconnectMode request so the CARD32 disconnect_mode field is filled from leftover bytes still sitting in the shared request buffer from a previous request, leaking residual request data (CWE-200). The swapped-client SProc only used REQUEST_AT_LEAST_SIZE, which still does not enforce an exact request length. The sibling GetClientDisconnectMode handler in the same file already used REQUEST_SIZE_MATCH, so the missing check is specific to Set.

round11_research.bug_semantics: In os/io.c ReadRequestFromClient, a Big Request's 32-bit length (CARD32 units of 4 bytes) from get_big_req_len is stored in unsigned int needed and converted to bytes with needed <<= 2 before the max-size check (historically MAXBUFSIZE, later needed > maxBigRequestSize << 2). A client-supplied length greater than UINT_MAX/4 wraps needed to a small byte count, so the bound appears to pass and the server continues with a truncated length (realloc/copy/dispatch), enabling memory corruption and DoS (CWE-190). A second identical <<= 2 after assembling a complete xBigReq has the same wrap. Local X client with Big Requests; CVSS AV:L/PR:L. Vendor (X.Org/Red Hat) rates this a real integer-overflow bypass of the size check.

round11_research.bug_semantics: In ReadRequestFromClient (os/io.c), an oversized Big Request is not disconnected; leftover payload is tracked as ConnectionInput.ignoreBytes and skipped instead of parsed. After consuming a request, if gotnow becomes 0 the same ConnectionInput buffer is published on AvailableInput and later recycled to another live client via FreeInputs. The share predicate historically checked only !gotnow, so a client that finished a request with leftover ignoreBytes could donate a buffer whose ignoreBytes was still nonzero. The next client then entered the ignoreBytes path and skipped its real request, hanging that client (DoS). CWE-667 / local authenticated availability. First-party fix: only set AvailableInput when !gotnow && !oci->ignoreBytes.
evidence: CVE.org record CVE-2025-49178 state=PUBLISHED (CNA Red Hat, datePublished 2025-06-17, dateUpdated 2026-06-30); GHSA-69rm-w9qj-3x45 withdrawn_at=null. Not rejected/withdrawn.

round11_research.bug_semantics: RandR RRChangeProviderProperty computes int total_size = total_len * size_in_bytes (size_in_bytes = format>>3) with no overflow guard, then malloc(total_size) and memcpy of len/prop_value->size times size_in_bytes. A local X client can issue RRChangeProviderProperty (ProcRRChangeProviderProperty) with format 8/16/32 and a large nUnits, or Append/Prepend onto an existing property so total_len = prop_value->size + len, wrapping the 32-bit int allocation size. The wrapped malloc is smaller than the subsequent copies, causing heap overflow (CWE-190) that Red Hat rates as memory corruption / possible code execution.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Bandit.Pipeline.determine_scheme/2 in lib/bandit/pipeline.ex copies a client-supplied request-target scheme into Plug.Conn.scheme and discards the transport secure? flag whenever the client provides any scheme. On a plaintext HTTP/1.1 listener, an unauthenticated client can send an RFC 9112 §3.2.2 absolute-form target such as GET https://victim/path HTTP/1.1; :erlang.decode_packet unwraps that as {:absoluteURI, :https, ...}, resolve_request_target!/2 stores {"https", host, port, path}, and determine_scheme returns "https". The same string arrives on h2c via the attacker-controlled :scheme pseudo-header (build_request_target!/2). Plug.Conn.Adapter.conn/5 then yields conn.scheme == :https despite no TLS. Downstream Plug.SSL can skip HTTP→HTTPS redirects, secure cookies can be emitted on plaintext, and CSRF/SameSite or audit logic that trusts conn.scheme is misled. At 1.10.4 the catch-all is still `{_, scheme} -> scheme` (pipeline.ex:84-91); 1.11.0 forces scheme from transport only.

round11_research.bug_semantics: CRI checkpoint restore (CreateContainer → CRImportCheckpoint) treats attacker-controlled checkpoint metadata as authoritative image identity. It reads RootfsImageRef/RootfsImageName from the checkpoint config.dump, pulls that ref, then ImageService.Create-tags the pulled content as RootfsImageName without verifying that the name matches the digest or that the caller is allowed to bind that local tag. A pod-create attacker can therefore inject a malicious image under an arbitrary NAME:TAG on the node; later pods using IfNotPresent/Never on the poisoned tag run the attacker image under the victim identity. ImageService.Create AlreadyExists is ignored, so a missing local tag is created; an existing NAME:TAG is not overwritten, but first-writer cache poisoning is enough.

round11_research.bug_semantics: In ALSA USB-audio implicit-feedback playback, snd_usb_handle_sync_urb() (sound/usb/endpoint.c) converts each inbound isochronous packet's actual_length into a playback frame count by dividing by the sync-source (sender) stride and writes that value straight into out_packet->packet_size[i] with no min() against ep->maxframesize. A connected USB audio device fully controls those IN packet lengths. Because playback then multiplies the stored frame count by the (often larger) playback stride, an oversized capture packet becomes an even larger outbound packet. The unclamped sizes are enqueued and memcpy'd into ctx->packet_size by snd_usb_queue_pending_output_urbs(), then consumed by prepare_playback_urb() (sound/usb/pcm.c) and prepare_silent_urb() to set urb->iso_frame_desc[].length and to memset/copy into the URB DMA buffer allocated as maxsize * packets. Before the Feb 2026 consumer-side cap, that produced URB submissions past the endpoint's hardware frame/packet limit and out-of-bounds writes into kernel-coherent USB buffers (C/I/A high via local USB gadget). The 2026-07-28 fix clamps the computed frame count at the store site in snd_usb_handle_sync_urb().

round11_research.bug_semantics: sch_teql keeps a circular singly linked list of slave qdiscs in teql_master->slaves / teql_sched_data->next. teql_qdisc_init() inserts, teql_destroy() unlinks, teql_master_xmit() rotates the head after a successful slave xmit or neighbour resolve, and teql_dequeue() also rewrites the head, all as plain pointer stores with no list lock and no RCU accessors. Concurrent RTM_NEWQDISC/RTM_DELQDISC on slaves (CAP_NET_ADMIN, including a user/netns) races with teql0 transmit: teql_destroy() can unlink a Qdisc that teql_master_xmit() still holds, the object is then freed after the qdisc RCU grace period, and the xmit walk (not in an RCU-bh read-side section covering that list) dereferences the stale pointer. KASAN: slab-use-after-free read of size 8 in teql_master_xmit of a freed kmalloc-512 qdisc. Attack path is local rtnetlink qdisc churn plus packet injection through teql0.

round11_research.bug_semantics: irdma_copy_user_pgaddrs walks every ib_umem DMA block and writes each address through *pbl, advancing the pointer with irdma_next_pbl_addr. The only explicit cap is if (++pbl_cnt == palloc->total_cnt) break. irdma_setup_pbles with lvl/use_pbles==0 skips irdma_get_pble, leaves the kzalloc-zeroed palloc->total_cnt at 0, and aims pbl at the 4-slot iwmr->pgaddrmem array (IRDMA_MAX_SAVED_PHY_PGADDR). Because pbl_cnt is pre-incremented from 0, it never equals total_cnt==0, so the loop continues until the umem is exhausted and writes attacker-controlled DMA addresses past pgaddrmem[4] into adjacent irdma_mr/iwpbl heap fields. For QP/CQ/SRQ, lvl is derived from a separate udata field (e.g. req.cq_pages > 1), so a local uverbs irdma_reg_user_mr caller can request the lvl==0 path while supplying a umem with more DMA blocks than the 4-entry array.

round11_research.bug_semantics: mac802154 treats local->interfaces (historically priv->slaves) as an RCU list: adds use list_add_tail_rcu(), single-interface removal uses list_del_rcu()+synchronize_rcu(), and ieee802154_wake_queue()/stop_queue()/disable_queue() walk the list under rcu_read_lock() with list_for_each_entry_rcu(). Bulk hardware teardown (ieee802154_remove_interfaces, originally the loop in ieee802154_unregister_device/unregister_hw) instead called list_del(), which poisons list_head next/prev (LIST_POISON*). An in-flight async xmit completion can therefore follow a poisoned node in ieee802154_wake_queue() (inlined from ieee802154_release_queue), producing a KASAN wild-memory-access/GPF at dead000000000218. Local CAP_NET_ADMIN in a user namespace can race AF_IEEE802154 sendmmsg against MAC802154_HWSIM_CMD_DEL_RADIO / driver unregister; the 2026 fix changes only the bulk path to list_del_rcu() and relies on the subsequent unregister_netdevice() RCU wait rather than an extra synchronize_rcu().

round11_research.bug_semantics: SiYuan publish mode stores two independent per-notebook/document flags on PublishAccessItem: Visible (listing/navigation) and Disable (forbid publish access). Reader-facing result filters in kernel/model/publish_access.go resolved their ignore list with GetInvisiblePublishAccess (!Visible only) and never consulted GetDisablePublishAccess. A document can be Visible=true and Disable=true at once; anonymous RoleReader callers of search, backlink, asset-content, saved-criteria, recent-docs, graph, and tag endpoints then received that forbidden content. The canonical block-tree check checkBlockTreeAccessableByPublishAccess already used GetDisablePublishAccess. CWE-863.

round11_research.bug_semantics: AzureKeyVaultBackend, in multi-team mode, looks up a Connection or Variable by first probing the caller's team-scoped vault name and, on miss, falling through to a team-agnostic lookup that uses the caller-supplied id as the secret name. A guard `_is_team_specific_accessed_as_global` was meant to stop an id that already names a team namespace, but it is gated on `team_name is None`, so it never runs for a team-scoped caller. A caller authorized for team A can therefore pass an id that spells out another team's namespace (after the TEAM_SEP refactor, e.g. `otherteam--secret`); the team-A probe misses and the fall-through returns that other team's credentials in full (CWE-639).

round11_research.bug_semantics: Apache Airflow EnvironmentVariablesBackend stored a team-scoped Connection or Variable as AIRFLOW_CONN__<TEAM>___<ID> / AIRFLOW_VAR__<TEAM>___<ID>. get_variable/get_conn_value probed only the caller's own namespace and then fell through to os.environ.get(PREFIX + id.upper()). Supplying the encoded identifier _<TEAM>___<ID> made that global read byte-identical to another team's namespaced variable. A later guard, _is_team_specific_accessed_as_global, was supposed to stop this but only ran when team_name is None and used re.fullmatch(r'_[^_]+___.+', secret_id), which cannot span a legal underscore-bearing team name (^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{3,50}$). With the guard inapplicable, an authenticated user of one team could have POST /api/v2/connections/test call Connection.get_connection_from_secrets(connection_id) and authenticate outward with the other team's credentials. Exploitation requires [core] multi_team, [core] test_connection=Enabled (ships Disabled), team-scoped secrets in the API-server environment, and knowledge of the encoded identifier.

round11_research.bug_semantics: picklescan classifies pickle GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL opcodes as Dangerous only when the (module, name) pair hits its denylist (_suspicious_globals, later renamed _unsafe_globals). logging.FileHandler was never on that denylist through v1.0.0, so a REDUCE payload that instantiates logging.FileHandler(path) scans without a Dangerous finding. Loading the pickle constructs FileHandler in default append mode: a missing path becomes a new zero-byte file at an attacker-chosen location (lock-file / filesystem-pollution DoS); an existing path is opened without overwrite. The scanner itself uses pickletools.genops rather than pickle.loads; the bypass is that downstream users who trust a clean/non-Dangerous scan then deserialize the file.

round11_research.bug_semantics: nltk.pathsec is the centralized I/O sentinel (path, file://, urlopen/SSRF, zip-slip, and pickle-adjacent loads). Through 3.9.4 it initialized ENFORCE=False, so every validation gate that detected an unauthorized path or URL emitted RuntimeWarning and then continued instead of raising PermissionError. With the default unset, pathsec.open('/etc/passwd') and equivalent untrusted loads succeed; NLTK_PATHSEC_ENFORCE / nltk.pathsec.ENFORCE=True is required to actually block. This is CWE-1188 (insecure default), not a missing check: the checks exist but fail open. First-party GHSA-p3m8-78j2-g5p3 (published, not withdrawn) and CVE-2026-62388 (CVE.org PUBLISHED) both name this default. Affected shipped range is the pathsec-bearing 3.9.4 line; 3.10.0 flips the default to ENFORCE=True.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Apache Airflow Task SDK deserialized JSON Variables and then dispatched masking on the top-level Python type. After json.loads, only str values (and, after CVE-2026-59244, dict values) were passed to mask_secret; a top-level list matched neither branch and was returned unmasked. Secrets stored as a JSON array therefore never entered the secrets masker, so they appeared in cleartext in task logs and in the Rendered Templates UI to any authenticated user who could read those views. add_mask already walked iterables under a supplied name, so nested lists inside a dict were masked; only a top-level list was skipped. The correct list handling is mask_secret(list, variable_key) so elements inherit the Variable key's sensitivity without anonymously over-masking ordinary values.

round11_research.bug_semantics: In multi-team mode, Apache Airflow's Amazon Secrets Manager and SSM Parameter Store backends look up a Connection or Variable by first building the caller's team-scoped AWS name (`{prefix}/{team}--{id}`) and, on a miss, falling through to the team-agnostic name (`{prefix}/{id}`). A guard `if team_name is None and re.fullmatch(r"[^-]+--.+", secret_id): return None` was meant to refuse ids that already spell out a team namespace, but the `team_name is None` conjunct makes it a no-op whenever a team scope is supplied — exactly the authorized-caller case. A caller in team A who supplies id `B--secret` therefore misses `prefix/A--B--secret` and then reads `prefix/B--secret`, obtaining team B's credentials in full (CWE-639). No extra config is required beyond multi-team mode plus either backend. A related prefix collision (team `a` asking for `b--c` builds the same name team `a--b` builds for `c`) is the same user-controlled id, settled by the same fix.

round11_research.bug_semantics: CWE-426/CWE-427 untrusted search path: two NLTK Graphviz helpers executed the `dot` program by bare name (`subprocess.Popen`/`subprocess.run` argv starting with `"dot"`), so the OS resolved the binary via PATH and, on Windows, the current working directory. An attacker who can plant a file named `dot` in CWD or a relative/writable PATH entry gets that binary executed instead of Graphviz (arbitrary code execution). At <=3.10.2, `nltk.parse.dependencygraph.dot2img` called `find_binary("dot")` but discarded the returned absolute path and still ran `["dot", ...]`; `nltk.translate.api.AlignedSent._repr_svg_` ran the bare name with no validation. `DependencyGraph._repr_svg_` had been refactored to call `dot2img`, so it inherited the same sink. The 3.10.3 fix runs the absolute path `find_binary` already returns (it refuses a CWD-relative match for a bare tool name).

round11_research.bug_semantics: POST /api/v2/assets/{asset_id}/materialize and the XCom result check inside wait_dag_run_until_finished call get_auth_manager().is_authorized_dag with DagDetails(id=dag_id) and team_name left at default None. round11_research.bug_semantics: CRuby Nokogiri::XML::Node#initialize_copy_with_args is a protected copy helper behind Node#dup and #clone. It unwraps its source argument with Noko_Node_Get_Struct, which is a DATA_PTR cast to xmlNodePtr and performs no Ruby type check. Namespace is not a Node subclass and wraps xmlNs, which is smaller than xmlNode. If application code send-calls the helper with a non-Node (the vendor test is Node.allocate.send(:initialize_copy_with_args, namespace, 1, doc)), the C code treats an xmlNs as an xmlNode; noko_xml_document_pin_node then reads node->doc past the xmlNs object, a heap out-of-bounds read that crashes the process (CWE-843). Public #dup/#clone pass self, which is a Node, so normal API use and untrusted document input cannot trigger it. Only CRuby is affected; JRuby uses asXmlNode. Nokogiri 1.19.4 raises TypeError via rb_obj_is_kind_of before the unwrap.

round11_research.bug_semantics: phpMyFAQ public child-resource APIs (GET /api/v3.1/comments/{recordId} and GET /api/v3.1/attachments/{recordId}) return comments and attachment metadata keyed only by numeric FAQ record ID, without checking whether the current requester can view that parent FAQ. round11_research.bug_semantics: When phpMyFAQ uses PostgreSQL through the native pgsql PHP extension, public FAQ search interpolates the unauthenticated `search` parameter into `Pgsql::search()` as `(%s) ILIKE ('%%%s%%')` after `SearchDatabase::escapeLikeWildcards()`. That helper prefixes user `%` and `_` with `|`, which only disables LIKE wildcards if the SQL also declares `ESCAPE '|'`. Native `Pgsql.php` did not: after the BIC it had no matching ESCAPE clause (PostgreSQL default escape is backslash), and after the later 4.1 merge it declared `ESCAPE '='`. In both states `|` is a literal, so attacker-supplied `%`/`_` stay active wildcards, forcing maximally broad ILIKE matches and expensive sequential scans (availability DoS). Quotes are still passed through `getDb()->escape()`, so this is not quote-breaking SQL injection. The PDO sibling `PdoPgsql.php` declares `ESCAPE '|'` and is not affected.

round11_research.bug_semantics: phpMyFAQ's authenticated content-backup API (BackupController::download type=content, gated by PermissionType::BACKUP) built a ZipArchive of PMF_CONTENT_DIR — including content/core/config/database.php — at the web-accessible document-root path PMF_ROOT_DIR/content.zip, then streamed the file and unlinked it. Unlike archives under content/, that root path is not blocked by content/.htaccess. An unauthenticated client can race GET /content.zip during the write-to-unlink window (or fetch a leftover archive after a failed unlink) and obtain database credentials and other content/. With admin-context XSS, an attacker can trigger the authenticated backup from the victim session and then fetch content.zip without holding BACKUP themselves.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated POST /api/parse-url fetches a caller-supplied URL, converts the HTML to Markdown, and returns the body. round11_research.bug_semantics: Nokogiri's CSS selector tokenizer (lib/nokogiri/css/tokenizer.rex, generated lib/nokogiri/css/tokenizer.rb) compiles CSS-2.1-style macros to Onigmo/Joni regular expressions. Three exponential-backtracking (CWE-1333) vectors share nested alternation under '*' plus {unicode}'s variable-length hex run \[0-9A-Fa-f]{1,6}. (1) STRING: the body class [^\n\r\f"] also matches '\', overlapping the {escape} branch, so unterminated input like [foo="\a\a\a... has 2**N parses. (2) STRING: each hex-escape position admits six lengths, so \aaaaaa\aaaaaa... has 6**N parses; missing the closing quote forces the engine to enumerate every parse before failing. (3) IDENT/FUNCTION: the same {1,6} length ambiguity sits under {nmchar}* in {ident}; when {ident}\({w} fails because no '(' follows an identifier-shaped prefix, payload \aaaaaa\aaaaaa...X backtracks through 6**N parses (n=10 ~11.4s). Attackers inject adversarial selectors into Nokogiri::CSS.xpath_for, Node#css, Node#at_css, Searchable#search, or CSS::Parser#parse. Affected: nokogiri < 1.19.3. Patched: 1.19.3, which wraps the STRING/nmchar/nmstart bodies in atomic groups (?>...) and excludes '\' from the string class.
evidence: First-party advisory GHSA-c4rq-3m3g-8wgx (published 2026-04-27, not withdrawn): three ReDoS vectors in the CSS tokenizer; affected nokogiri < 1.19.3; patched 1.19.3; public sinks Nokogiri::CSS.xpath_for, Node#css, Node#at_css, Searchable#search, CSS::Parser#parse; Vector 1 reported by colby-swandale, Vectors 2-3 found by flavorjones.

round11_research.bug_semantics: CRuby Nokogiri::XSLT::Stylesheet#transform (ext/nokogiri/xslt_stylesheet.c) heap-allocates a NULL-terminated const char** params array, then converts each Ruby transform parameter with StringValueCStr before xsltApplyStylesheet. StringValueCStr raises ArgumentError on an embedded NUL; that raise skipped free/ruby_xfree of the array, leaking about 24–32 bytes per call. Attacker-controlled transform params containing null bytes can therefore grow RSS in a long-running process (CWE-401 DoS). The transform still raises as expected and does not corrupt memory. JRuby is unaffected. Fixed in 1.19.3 by populating params under rb_protect and ruby_xfree'ing before rb_jump_tag.

round11_research.bug_semantics: WebAuthn login is replayable because the per-login challenge never becomes server-side state. prepareForLogin() generates a challenge and mutates the stored-key JSON by reference, and authenticate() is supposed to compare the assertion against that stored challenge then burn it. Both login-prepare and login callers treat the mutated string as a local, never calling User::setWebAuthnKeys(), so the next login re-reads keys that register() persisted with only {key,id} and no challenge. authenticate() then fails open: if (!isset($key->challenge)) the anti-replay throw is skipped, and the only other challenge check compares attacker-supplied originalChallenge against attacker-supplied clientData. A captured successful assertion therefore authenticates indefinitely without the hardware key.

round11_research.bug_semantics: FramenetCorpusReader and NKJPCorpusReader build XML filesystem paths from caller-supplied selectors or poisoned corpus-index fields and open them with XMLCorpusView/builtin open(), bypassing CorpusReader.open() and nltk.pathsec. frame_by_name interpolates fn_fname into <root>/<frame_dir>/<name>.xml; doc() interpolates a fulltext index filename; lu/_lu_file interpolates an LU id into lu<id>.xml; NKJP add_root concatenates self.root+fileid and header/raw/words/sents read it. A ../ sequence, absolute path, or unsafe index component escapes the corpus root so those public methods parse and return outside-root XML. Affected: nltk < 3.10.0 (3.9.4 reproduced). CWE-73/CWE-22.

round11_research.bug_semantics: vLLM's video MediaIO merges unauthenticated request-level media_io_kwargs into the decode backend. VideoMediaIO.merge_kwargs() strips a requested video_backend/backend only when VIDEO_LOADER_REGISTRY.backend_requires_gpu(name) is true; that lookup defaults unknown names to False. DeepStream/NVDEC was implemented as DeepStreamVideoBackendMixin on the loader registered as "opencv" and was never registered with requires_gpu=True (unlike pynvvideocodec). A client can therefore set media_io_kwargs.video.backend=deepstream, pass the GPU-backend gate, and reach VideoBackend.load_bytes(). The DeepStream branch lazily constructs a process-wide DecodePool whose size is taken from request pool_size (clamped to 1–16; first request wins) and calls probe_metadata() for width/height but never _check_frame_pixel_limit(), so videos rejected by OpenCV/PyAV/TorchCodec/PyNvVideoCodec are GPU-decoded and starve concurrent work (partial CWE-400 DoS; CVSS 5.3).

round11_research.bug_semantics: Renovate's npm manager generateLockFile() builds lockfile-update commands as single shell strings. User-influenced packageName values (and workspace directory names) are concatenated into `npm install ...` without quoting. util/exec spawn() forces shell:true, so shell metacharacters in packageName execute as commands on the Renovate host. round11_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated SQL injection (CWE-89) in Camaleon CMS PostUniqValidator. Creating or editing a post with editor/author privileges submits post[slug]; the validator splits record.slug via translations_array and interpolates each fragment s into an ActiveRecord where() fragment as posts.slug LIKE '%-->#{s}<!--%'. Only the equality arm (slug = ?) is bound. A crafted slug with SQL metacharacters is therefore compiled into the uniqueness query, enabling boolean- or union-style blind extraction (and limited modification) of SQLite application tables, including admin credentials and configuration. Draft posts skip the check; published/pending posts hit it on save.

round11_research.bug_semantics: CWE-1321 prototype pollution in multipart/form-data parsing only. AdonisJS BodyParser feeds attacker-controlled multipart field names into FormFields.add(), which does lodash.set/get on a plain object store (`this._fields = {}` originally; later `#fields: any = {}`) without rejecting reserved keys. A field such as `__proto__.polluted` or `constructor.prototype.polluted` therefore writes onto Object.prototype at runtime. The sink at the patched versions is Multipart.#handleField(key, value) → FormFields.add(key, value) (and file fieldName via the same class). JSON and application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies use other parsers (qs/co-body) and are out of scope. Impact is unexpected behavior, logic bypass, or further issues depending on how polluted prototypes are later consumed. Affected: @adonisjs/bodyparser <= 10.1.2 and 11.0.0-next.0 .. 11.0.0-next.8. Patched by switching the store to Object.create(null) in 10.1.3 and 11.0.0-next.9.

round11_research.bug_semantics: MultipartFile.move(location, options) treats the attacker-controlled multipart filename as the destination basename. When options.name is omitted, the method defaults to this.clientName (the Content-Disposition filename) and builds the path with path.join(location, name) with no sanitization, prefix check, or basename() confinement. A crafted filename containing ../ (or an absolute path, which path.join can treat as the new root) writes the uploaded body outside the intended directory. After 900627c1500bb38155ee3f9620a89ed7609b996e the overwrite default is true, so an existing target is replaced. Reachable whenever an app calls move() without an explicit sanitized name.

round11_research.bug_semantics: CWE-915 mass assignment in @adonisjs/lucid BaseModel.merge() (propagating to fill/create/updateOrCreate and bulk writers) and later $consumeAdapterResult(). After column/relation checks, any payload key that passes this.hasOwnProperty(key) is assigned with this[key] = value. Internal ORM fields ($attributes, $original, $isPersisted, $isDeleted, $preloaded, $extras, $sideloaded, fillInvoked, forceUpdate, and similar) are initialized as own instance properties, so they satisfy that check. Unfiltered input such as request.all() can therefore set $isPersisted and force save() down the UPDATE path, overwrite $attributes/$original, or flip $isDeleted. Applications that drop unknown keys with a strict allowlist are not affected.

After NCBC-3173, ConnectionFactory and CouchbaseHttpClientFactory installed that callback whenever Kv/HttpCertificateCallbackValidation was null: IgnoreNameMismatch only short-circuited the ignore-true path, then ValidateWithDefaultCertificates/GetValidatorWithPredefinedCertificates returned chain.Build(cert) and never consulted the name-mismatch bit. A MITM with any cert chaining to the trusted/Capella CA therefore passed hostname verification. Compounding this, ClusterOptions.ForceIpAsTargetHost defaulted to true (NCBC-2959; IP was hardcoded as AuthenticateAsClient targetHost from SDK3 SSL wiring), so even .NET's built-in name check was bound to the peer IP rather than the configured hostname.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2025-49015 state=PUBLISHED (not rejected/withdrawn); GHSA-px2c-r924-mwcc withdrawn_at=null; CNA description matches hostname verification plus default IP-as-target-host.

round11_research.bug_semantics: CWE-400/CWE-770 DoS in @adonisjs/bodyparser PartHandler file-type detection: while MultipartFile.extname is still undefined, reportProgress concatenates every incoming multipart chunk into an in-memory detection buffer and re-runs magic-number detection. After the bound was dropped, getFileType returned null for the entire streaming path whenever content did not match a known signature (force=false on every chunk), so the buffer grew with the upload instead of stopping around file-type.minimumBytes (~4100). With deferred validations or a permissive size limit the stream is never short-circuited, and a public multipart endpoint can be crashed by a large or unbounded part whose body is not a known magic type (e.g. a fake .png of 0x41 bytes).

round11_research.bug_semantics: In setuid mode, singularity.conf 'limit container paths' is enforced by Image.AuthorizedPath on the container image path. Through SingularityCE 4.4.1 the check was strings.HasPrefix(i.Path, filepath.EvalSymlinks(filepath.Clean(limit))). That is a string-prefix test, not a directory-tree test, so a limit of /data/safe also authorizes sibling paths such as /data/safe-but-unsafe and /tmp/foo vs /tmp/foobar. filepath.Clean strips a trailing slash, so administrators cannot close the hole by writing /data/safe/. A low-privileged user who can place an image in a similarly named sibling directory bypasses the admin allowlist. The 4.4.2 fix compares filepath.Rel(limit, image) and accepts only '.' or filepath.IsLocal(rel).

round11_research.bug_semantics: FormFields.add() in @adonisjs/bodyparser copies unauthenticated multipart field names into lodash.set/get via @poppinss/utils. CVE-2026-25754 / GHSA-f5x2-vj4h-vg4c was 'fixed' by changing the root store from {} to Object.create(null), which only stops first-segment payloads such as __proto__.polluted and constructor.prototype.polluted. lodash.set still materializes intermediate objects as plain {}, so nested keys (user.__proto__.polluted, user[__proto__][polluted], user.constructor.prototype.polluted2) write onto Object.prototype process-wide. Any route behind BodyParserMiddleware that accepts multipart/form-data is an unauthenticated remote sink. Affected published ranges are >=10.1.3 <10.1.5 and >=11.0.0-next.9 <11.0.3; v11.0.2 still carries Object.create(null) without path-segment rejection even though the GHSA text stops at 11.0.1. Closure rejects keys whose lodash.toPath() segments include __proto__, prototype, or constructor.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Rainbond region API broken access control / cross-enterprise IDOR (CWE-639). round11_research.bug_semantics: Kroki's Vega convert() JSON-parses a caller-supplied diagram spec and passes it to vega.View(vega.parse(spec)). Vega's loader then fetches any data URL in that spec, including file:// paths. With KROKI_SAFE_MODE=secure (the default), convert() only rejected spec.data when it was an array of objects that had a url field. A native Vega spec whose data was a single object (data.url, e.g. file:///etc/passwd) or whose group marks carried their own datasets (marks[].data[].url) skipped the guard, so an unauthenticated /vega request could SSRF or read local files (CWE-552).

round11_research.bug_semantics: When an ActiveMQArtemis Custom Resource omits admin/cluster credentials, the operator auto-fills AMQ_USER, AMQ_PASSWORD, AMQ_CLUSTER_USER, and AMQ_CLUSTER_PASSWORD from process-global package variables populated once in environments.init() (environments.Defaults / GLOBAL_AMQ_CLUSTER_*). Those values are then copied into each CR's credentials Secret and broker env. Distinct CRs therefore receive the same starting credentials for the lifetime of the operator process (CWE-1391). A local low-privilege observer who can read one generated Secret can reuse the same user/password against other CR-managed brokers. Red Hat Bugzilla 2362827 states the four AMQ_* fields do not regenerate between separate CR instances.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Bitcoinrb's experimental SPV RPC HTTP server (lib/bitcoin/rpc/http_server.rb) parses a POST JSON body into method/params and dispatches with Ruby Object#send(command, *args) while including RequestHandler. There is no allowlist that command is an intended RPC method, so a client can invoke Kernel#eval / Kernel#system (and any other reachable method) with attacker-controlled arguments. The published PoC POSTs {"method":"eval","params":["File.write(\"/tmp/pwned\",\"owned\")"]} to the EventMachine listener (binds 0.0.0.0:8332 by default). The sink is the unvalidated send of JSON method plus splatted JSON params; CWE-77 as reviewed by GHSA-q66h-m87m-j2q6. Separately, the type-1 readClassDescriptor path called Class.forName(className, true, classLoader) after the allow-list check, so an allow-listed class name still ran <clinit> during descriptor resolution before any instance was built (ZDRES-233).

round11_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated CWE-639 IDOR in the Calendar Event Frontend Dialog. GET /ccm/calendar/view_event/{bID}/{occurrence_id} is handled by Concrete\Controller\Dialog\Frontend\Event, which extends Backend\UserInterface so shouldRunControllerTask()/getViewObject() call canAccess(); that method always returns true. view() only requires Block::getByID($bID) to be a calendar block, then loads EventOccurrence::getByID($occurrence_id) with no check that the occurrence belongs to the block's calendar and no canViewCalendar() on either the block calendar or the occurrence's calendar. Fixed in 9.5.1 by requiring canViewCalendar() on the block-bound calendar before loading the occurrence.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Alist's DefaultConfig() set TlsInsecureSkipVerify to true, so first-run config.json and any upgrade whose config.json lacked that key inherited skip-verify. round11_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated Magento GraphQL (frontName graphql) accepts a query document and executes it through QueryProcessor::process without bounding field aliases. An attacker POSTs a document that aliases expensive operations (for example many products selections) so each alias independently runs a costly resolver. Pre-fix production-mode checks only ran QueryComplexityLimiter::validateFieldCount plus webonyx QueryComplexity/QueryDepth (defaults queryComplexity=1000, queryDepth=20), which still allow a large number of aliased root fields under the field budget and do not stop alias-driven resource exhaustion. That is CWE-20 improper input validation leading to application DoS (CVSS AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N, no admin). APSB25-71 added validateAliasCount (default maximum_alias_allowed=10) as a preliminary check before those validators.

round11_research.bug_semantics: AbstractIoBuffer.getObject() deserializes untrusted Java native serialization streams. The CVE-2024-52046 classname allowlist (acceptMatchers) was applied too late: readClassDescriptor() still executed Class.forName(className, true, classLoader) before any matcher check, so a disallowed class's static initializer could already have run; resolveClass() then consulted acceptMatchers only after ObjectStreamClass.forClass() was already non-null. round11_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated CWE-22 path traversal in Alist file-operation handlers. After the request directory is scoped to the caller's BasePath (originally stdpath.Join(user.BasePath, dir), later user.JoinPath which rejects '..' in the directory via utils.JoinBasePath), filename fields req.Names / renameObject.SrcName are concatenated with that directory using path.Join or fmt.Sprintf. Go path.Join cleans '..', so a name such as '../admin/private.txt' escapes the authorized directory and remove/copy/move/rename files belonging to other users on the same storage mount. PoC: POST /api/fs/remove with {"dir":"/","names":["../admin/private.txt"]}.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated GraphQL IDOR in QuoteGraphQl estimateTotals: Magento\QuoteGraphQl\Model\Resolver\EstimateTotals::resolve maps a caller-supplied masked cart_id through MaskedQuoteIdToQuoteId and returns the full Cart model (email, addresses, items, totals) without QuoteGraphQl GetCartForUser ownership/store checks. A network attacker who already knows a logged-in customer's 32-character masked quote id (AC:H; Adobe: conditions beyond attacker control) can invoke the anonymous estimateTotals mutation, load that customer's quote, and read high-sensitivity cart/PII. Integrity is not the scored impact (I:N); the mutation also runs TotalsInformationManagement::calculate, but the CWE-863 bypass is the missing cart-owner authorization before the Cart is returned.

round11_research.bug_semantics: CVE-2025-54236 (SessionReaper) is nested object instantiation in Magento's REST/WebAPI deserializer. Magento\Framework\Webapi\ServiceInputProcessor::_createFromArray hydrates API JSON by (1) reflecting the target class constructor and (2) recursively calling convertValue() on matching payload keys. Until the APSB25-88 whitelist, getConstructorData() accepted any constructor parameter type, so an unauthenticated PUT to endpoints such as /rest/default/V1/guest-carts/{id}/order could nest Magento\Framework\Session\Config through payment/session constructor graphs and set session.save_path. Combined with the unauthenticated /customer/address_file/upload primitive, that yields session takeover and, on file-based session storage, PHP session deserialization RCE. The 2025 fix skips constructor parameters unless the type is simple or matches *\Api\Data\*.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2025-54236 state=PUBLISHED (CNA Adobe, datePublished 2025-09-09, dateUpdated 2025-10-24); not rejected/withdrawn. round11_research.bug_semantics: In Apache Cassandra 5.0 mTLS (MutualTlsAuthenticator), ADD IDENTITY maps a client-certificate identity onto a role used for authentication. AddIdentityStatement.authorize() checked Permission.CREATE on the caller's own primary role (state.getUser().getPrimaryRole()) and never inspected the target role. execute() then called RoleManager.addIdentity(identity, role) with the CQL-supplied role and no further authorization. A user granted CREATE on roles (for example GRANT CREATE ON ALL ROLES, which satisfies CREATE on the caller's primary role) could therefore bind their certificate identity to an arbitrary existing role, including a superuser such as cassandra, and then authenticate as that role. The same first-write also left DROP IDENTITY checking DROP only on the caller's primary role. CreateRoleStatement in the same tree already required CREATE on RoleResource.root() and forbade non-superusers from creating superuser roles; ADD IDENTITY omitted both controls.

round11_research.bug_semantics: rancher/local-path-provisioner loads helperPod.yaml from the local-path-config ConfigMap (or --helper-pod-file), YAML-to-JSON-unmarshals it into a v1.Pod, DeepCopies that object in createHelperPod, then creates the pod on the target node during PVC provision/delete. Until v0.0.36 the loader accepted any pod spec: privileged securityContext, extra hostPath volumes, capability adds, hostNetwork/PID/IPC, custom serviceAccountName, initContainers, envFrom, and lifecycle hooks all survived into the created HelperPod. A principal who can edit that ConfigMap can therefore plant a privileged helper with host root mounted and steal node files or other pods' ServiceAccount tokens on the next volume operation.

round11_research.bug_semantics: cqlsh records every executed statement in a local readline history file and never redacts secrets. Commands such as LOGIN <user> '<password>', CREATE/ALTER USER|ROLE ... WITH PASSWORD, and other password-bearing CQL therefore persist in cleartext in ~/.cassandra/cqlsh_history (migrated from ~/.cqlsh_history). Anyone with local read access to that file recovers prior-session credentials. CVE.org and Apache (CASSANDRA-21180 / oss-security) treat this as a real CWE-532 leak in Cassandra 4.0.0–4.0.19, not a withdrawn or rejected record. The 4.0.20 vendor patch does not strip passwords from history; it adds --disable-history / cqlshrc [history] disabled=true, skips readline.write_history_file when disabled, and prints a warning that history may contain passwords.

round11_research.bug_semantics: When phpseclib validates an untrusted X.509 certificate, X509::validateSignature() (caonly=true by default) falls through to testForIntermediate() if the issuer is not already in the CA store. That helper reads the AIA caIssuers uniformResourceIdentifier straight from the certificate and fetchURL() does fsockopen() to the attacker-chosen host and port with no loopback/private/link-local/metadata or port restriction. URL fetching is enabled by default (disable_url_fetch=false; disableURLFetch() is opt-out). The fetched body is used only if it parses as a certificate, so the impact is CWE-918 SSRF / internal recon rather than direct response disclosure.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Apache MINA IoBuffer.getObject() deserializes with a custom ObjectInputStream. After the CVE-2024-52046 allowlist, AbstractIoBuffer.resolveClass() still had two branches: if ObjectStreamClass.forClass() was non-null it consulted acceptMatchers, but if forClass() was null (primitive/type-0 and other unresolved descriptors) it called Class.forName(name, false, classLoader) with no filter. An attacker who can supply serialized bytes to getObject() therefore bypasses the classname allowlist and can cause arbitrary class loading / gadget deserialization (CWE-502 RCE). The 2026 patch applies acceptMatchers before any Class.forName, on both branches.

round11_research.bug_semantics: AES-CBC decrypt (default mode) PKCS#7-style unpads by reading the last plaintext byte as pad length and taking a data-dependent path when that length is invalid (0 or greater than the block size). In the pre-fix form the length predicate used boolean `||`, which short-circuits so a zero pad byte skips `$length > $this->block_size`; valid vs invalid padding therefore differ in both control flow and wall-clock time, and invalid padding later returns false / throws instead of the stripped plaintext. A chosen-ciphertext attacker who can observe decrypt timing (or the validity signal) can recover CBC plaintext (CWE-208 padding-oracle timing).

round11_research.bug_semantics: Tor conflux shares one conflux_t (cfx) across all legs of a set. linked_circuit_closed() removes a closing linked leg and, when it is the last remaining leg, deletes the cfx from the linked pool but deliberately leaves circ->conflux pointing at that still-alive object so linked_circuit_free() can free it later. A recovery leg for the same nonce (conflux_launch_leg -> unlinked_get_or_create) reuses that same cfx with is_for_linked_set. When the recovery leg later finishes linking (conflux_process_linked -> try_finalize_set -> cfx_add_leg), it re-adds the cfx to the linked pool and sets recovery->circ->conflux to it, creating two distinct circuits that both own the same object: the already-closed last original leg (not yet reaped) and the revived recovery leg. On post-loop reap, linked_circuit_free() on the first empty-legs circuit calls conflux_free(cfx); the second circuit then dereferences circ->conflux->legs (heap UAF) and would otherwise conflux_free again (double free). A malicious exit can drive link -> recover -> close last linked leg -> relink recovery -> close/reap to crash the client. CWE-911 / TROVE-2026-026 / bug 41306.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-77587 state=PUBLISHED (cveawg.mitre.org, datePublished 2026-08-20, not rejected/withdrawn). Affected torproject/Tor from 0.4.8.1-alpha lessThan 0.4.9.11. GHSA-9mf5-x83c-fg2x withdrawn_at=null; GitHub advisory withdrawn_at is not authoritative here anyway.

round11_research.bug_semantics: conflux_send_switch_command() encodes a RELAY_COMMAND_CONFLUX_SWITCH cell and calls relay_send_command_from_edge() without checking the return. That helper packages the cell onto the circuit queue and, on failure, logs, calls circuit_mark_for_close(), and returns -1. Closing a conflux leg runs conflux_circuit_has_closed() -> cfx_del_leg(), which NULLs cfx->curr_leg when it matches the closing leg and tor_free()s the leg object. conflux_decide_circ_for_send() has already swapped cfx->curr_leg to the new hop and, treating the SWITCH send as success, writes cfx->curr_leg->last_seq_sent; after the free/NULL that store is a NULL write after free and crashes. CWE-252 (unchecked return) is the direct defect; the crash is TROVE-2026-017 / bug 41263.

round11_research.bug_semantics: A Tor onion-service client accepted a RENDEZVOUS_ESTABLISHED cell from the rendezvous point based only on circuit purpose CIRCUIT_PURPOSE_C_ESTABLISH_REND, without recording whether it had actually sent ESTABLISH_RENDEZVOUS. hs_ident is allocated with tor_malloc_zero, and both the 20-byte rendezvous cookie and the client ntor keypair are filled only inside hs_circ_send_establish_rendezvous (which also regenerates them on every call). If that send is skipped, raced, or has not yet happened—client_rendezvous_circ_has_opened can return early when node_supports_v3_rendezvous_point fails, and circuit_get_open_circ_or_launch can call circuit_has_opened on an already-open cannibalized rend circuit—the RP can inject an unsolicited RENDEZVOUS_ESTABLISHED. The client then marks the circuit C_REND_READY and may emit INTRODUCE1 with a still-zero cookie/keypair, after which the RP can complete RENDEZVOUS2 as if it were the onion service (CWE-362).
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-77638 state=PUBLISHED (not rejected/withdrawn); CNA MITRE; affected torproject Tor from 0.3.5.3-alpha before 0.4.9.11; CWE-362; description matches GHSA-pq38-gw56-4w65; GHSA withdrawn_at is null. https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-77638

round11_research.bug_semantics: networkstatus_parse_detached_signatures and networkstatus_parse_vote_from_string accept any digest name crypto_digest_algorithm_parse_name understands (sha1=0, sha256=1, sha512=2, sha3-256=3, sha3-512=4) after only testing a<0, then use that digest_algorithm_t as an index into common_digests_t.d[N_COMMON_DIGEST_ALGORITHMS][DIGEST256_LEN] where N_COMMON_DIGEST_ALGORITHMS is DIGEST_SHA256+1 (two slots). An additional-digest line with alg sha3-256/sha512/sha3-512 therefore does an out-of-bounds write through base16_decode(digests->d[alg], ...) plus an OOB read in tor_mem_is_zero/fast_mem_is_zero(digests->d[alg], ...); a consensus directory-signature with an unexpected Algorithm stores sig->alg and later networkstatus_check_document_signature OOB-reads consensus->digests.d[sig->alg]. Unauthenticated consensus or detached-signature documents can trigger it (CWE-787). Impact is minor for most Tor roles and potentially major for directory authorities (TROVE-2026-019 / tor#41267).
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-77642 state=PUBLISHED (not rejected/withdrawn); GHSA-36cc-rhpv-jrxc withdrawn_at=null; NVD/GHSA summary matches TROVE-2026-019. round11_research.bug_semantics: PHProxy's intended SSRF control for user-supplied proxy targets is a hostname-string regex blacklist ($_hosts, default '#^127\.|192\.168\.|10\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.|localhost#i') applied with preg_match against parse_url() host only. Unauthenticated callers supply the target via the configured URL parameter (url_var_name; '_proxurl' in v1.1.1 and HEAD). A hostname that does not literally match those prefixes (PoC: a public DNS name such as vul.aegisrisk.xyz bound to 127.0.0.1) is allowed, after which the proxy opens a server-side HTTP(S) connection to the resolved internal address. That bypasses the blacklist and reaches loopback/RFC1918 services (CWE-918). CVE-2025-52362 / GHSA-37c4-9pw5-3r33 (published, not withdrawn) affect v1.1.1 and prior.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Public safe ruint::algorithms::div::reciprocal_mg10 is a 256-entry MG10 reciprocal lookup. Callers must pass d >= 2^63 so that d9 = d >> 55 is in [256, 511] and (d9 - 256) indexes TABLE. The only guard is debug_assert!(d >= (1 << 63)), which is compiled out in release. The live load is unsafe TABLE.get_unchecked((d9.0 - 256) as usize). Passing d = 0 (or any d < 2^63) makes d9 < 256; the unsigned subtraction wraps to a huge usize and get_unchecked reads outside TABLE, which is UB/memory corruption in safe Rust. The function is re-exported as algorithms::div::reciprocal and is callable by downstream crates.

round11_research.bug_semantics: In examples/acf-can/linux/acf-can-listener.c, num_can_msgs is a uint8_t assigned from int avtp_to_can(), which returns -1 on rejection (wrong subtype, stream-id mismatch, invalid ACF, failed Avtp_Can_IsValid, or EFF/CAN-ID inconsistency). The conversion truncates -1 to 255. The subsequent write loop then iterates 255 times over the 15-slot stack array frame_t can_frames[MAX_CAN_FRAMES_IN_ACF] and write()s each slot to the CAN socket, leaking ~18 KB of adjacent stack as ~240 CAN frames. An unauthenticated UDP datagram with the default stream id 0xAABBCCDDEEFF0001 that later fails parsing is sufficient; no authentication exists on this path.

round11_research.bug_semantics: CVE-2026-73522 is a CWE-121 stack buffer overflow in Open1722's ACF-CAN example listener. avtp_to_can() in examples/acf-can/acf-can-common.c walks every ACF-CAN message in a received AVTP/UDP datagram and writes into can_frames[i++] with no capacity argument and no bound against MAX_CAN_FRAMES_IN_ACF (15). round11_research.bug_semantics: containerd CRI StartContainer, for Kubernetes pods with user namespaces (hostUsers:false / NamespaceMode_POD), called updateContainerIOOwner and appended containerd.WithUIDOwner/WithGIDOwner as NewTask options so shim stdio pipes matched the mapped host UID/GID. Pre-fix NewTask option helpers allocated a fresh empty runc options.Options whenever TaskInfo.Options was nil, then NewTask marshaled that object as the shim Create options, replacing the container's runtime options. With SystemdCgroup=true (typical kubelet/containerd), that dropped the systemd cgroup driver flag, so runc treated the systemd-style CgroupsPath as a cgroupfs name and placed the container under system.slice (or another default slice) instead of kubepods.slice. Sandbox/pause stayed in the pod hierarchy; workload containers escaped Kubernetes cpu/memory limits and could DoS the node. v2.0.0 did not take this CRI path; the issue reproduces from 2.0.1 through 2.0.4 with the systemd driver.

round11_research.bug_semantics: containerd CRI Attach (kubectl attach / CRI pods/attach) registers the client's stdout/stderr writers on ContainerIO writer groups and then blocks a monitor goroutine (Attach.func1 / attachStream) on a WriteCloseInformer close channel with a bare `<-close`. That channel is signaled only when the writer-group later Closes/Removes the informer (container stdout/stderr EOF, stdin-copy teardown, or a write error). If the attached container produces no further stdout/stderr, client disconnect never drives a Write, so Close is never observed. Attach also ignored the streaming HTTP/gRPC request context, so ctx cancellation could not unblock the wait, remove the writer-group entry, or return from wg.Wait(). Repeated Attach calls therefore leak those goroutines and their stack/heap, exhausting host memory (CWE-401).

round11_research.bug_semantics: In applyNaive (pkg/archive/tar.go), image unpack previously called fs.RootPath live for every tar entry so parent paths were re-walked and re-bounded to the unpack root. CVE-2025-47290 is a sequential TOCTOU (CWE-367) introduced when those RootPath results were memoized in cachedRootPath.get: after the first walk of a parent path, later entries reuse the cached lexical path and then create/link through it. A crafted layer can create a directory, have its resolved path cached as in-root, replace that directory with a symlink (or otherwise mutate the tree), and then unpack further names under the stale cached parent so kernel path resolution follows the symlink out of the unpack root onto the host filesystem. round11_research.bug_semantics: For a private 802.1X (WPA-Enterprise) profile (connection.permissions / priv->private_user), NetworkManager already reads FILE-typed cert/key properties as the owning user and hands them to wpa_supplicant as blobs. 802-1x.ca-path and 802-1x.phase2-ca-path are directories, so they cannot be blobs and were still emitted as raw ca_path/ca_path2 strings. With no ca-cert set, wpa_supplicant trusts that directory alone and still reports the authentication server as verified. An unprivileged local user with settings.modify.own can therefore point a private profile at an attacker-controlled CA directory, bypass server certificate validation, and steal EAP credentials via a rogue AP. CWE-863; incomplete CVE-2025-9615 private_user restriction, not a withdrawn advisory.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated CWE-434 RCE via POST /admin/tinymce/upload (admin.tinymce.upload). TinyMCEController::storeMedia() accepted any uploaded file, stored it on Laravel's default public disk under tinymce/, and returned Storage::url() so the file was web-reachable. No MIME/extension allowlist existed. At introduction the sink was $file->store('tinymce') (Laravel hashName/guessExtension); libmagic reports a PHP one-liner as text/x-php, so a crafted .php payload was persisted as a public .php object. On 2.2.x (including PoC commit ba25b7e7) the same sink used getClientOriginalExtension() plus storeAs, so the client-supplied .php suffix was kept even if Content-Type was spoofed as image/jpeg. Bouncer exempts this route from ACL, so any logged-in staff user can upload a webshell and execute it with a GET to /storage/tinymce/<file>.php.

round11_research.bug_semantics: MessagePack Lz4Block/Lz4BlockArray decompression feeds attacker-controlled LZ4 bytes into a vendored LZ4 r93 fast decoder (LZ4_uncompress_32/64) that accepts only destination length. round11_research.bug_semantics: In `anyquery server` (MySQL-protocol TCP listener, default port 8070), the SQLite namespace used by every client connection registers built-in virtual-table modules (`json_reader`/`csv_reader`, later `log_reader` and other `read_*` modules) that take a caller-supplied path/URL and open it through `hashicorp/go-getter` with no directory allowlist. Auth is optional: if neither AuthFile nor Users is set, the server accepts any connection. A remote client can therefore `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE ... USING csv_reader('/etc/passwd')` (or `json_reader` / `log_reader` / `file=...`) and `SELECT` the contents of any file the server process can read. Default `--host` is loopback, but `--host 0.0.0.0` (the advisory PoC) exposes the sink on the network with no sandbox.

round11_research.bug_semantics: CWE-674 uncontrolled recursion in MessagePack-CSharp JSON conversion (not typed MessagePack deserialization). ConvertFromJson's FromJsonCore recursively walks nested JSON objects and arrays without consulting MessagePackSecurity.MaximumObjectGraphDepth, so attacker-controlled nesting can exhaust the call stack. TinyJsonReader.ReadNextToken self-recurses on comma and colon separators, so even malformed JSON with long separator runs consumes one stack frame per character before structural validation. ConvertToJson applies DepthStep to arrays and maps, but the typeless ext-100 branch recursively calls ToJsonCore without DepthStep, so nested typeless wrappers bypass UntrustedData. Each path yields an uncatchable StackOverflowException instead of a bounded parse/serialization failure.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Anyquery server mode (`anyquery server`) binds a MySQL-protocol TCP port and, by default, authenticates with AuthServerNone when --auth-file is empty. Every SQLite connection registers built-in virtual-table modules (json_reader, csv_reader, later log_reader and others). Those modules take a caller-supplied file/URL argument and pass it to openMmapedFile/downloadFile, which builds a HashiCorp go-getter Client with no scheme, IP, or metadata-address restriction and fetches the source. An unauthenticated client can therefore CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE t USING log_reader('http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/') (or json_reader with the same URL) and SELECT the response, using the server as an SSRF proxy to loopback, RFC1918, and cloud metadata.

round11_research.bug_semantics: GuardDog extracted untrusted ZIP/wheel members with ZipFile.extract(member, path=os.path.join(target_directory, member)). extract() treats path as a trusted directory and then appends a sanitized member name; putting the raw member into path therefore skips zipfile's traversal stripping, double-appends the filename, and can write outside the intended extract directory when scanning a malicious PyPI package.

round11_research.bug_semantics: UnsafeBlitFormatterBase.Deserialize (Unity blit resolvers) reads an attacker-controlled inner byteLength from a MessagePack extension body and allocates new T[byteLength / elementSize] before checking that value against the already-bounded extension header length or remaining payload bytes. A tiny ext payload can declare an enormous byteLength, forcing a huge T[] allocation (CWE-770) on UnityBlitResolver / UnityBlitWithPrimitiveArrayResolver paths used for vectors, matrices, and primitive arrays. CVE-2026-48514 / GHSA-w567-gjr2-hm5j is PUBLISHED (not withdrawn/rejected) and is fixed by rejecting negative, unaligned, or mismatched byteLength before allocation.

round11_research.bug_semantics: MessagePackReader.ReadDateTime deserializes a timestamp extension by calling MessagePackPrimitives.TryReadDateTime, which sets tokenSize = checked((int)header.Length) from the attacker-controlled MessagePack extension body length and returns DecodeResult.InsufficientBuffer when the current span is shorter than that size, before checking that only the legal timestamp encodings (4, 8, or 12 bytes) are present. The reader's InsufficientBuffer slow path then does stackalloc byte[tokenSize]. A tiny Ext32 payload can therefore declare a huge timestamp body, force a single-frame stack allocation large enough to throw an uncatchable StackOverflowException, and terminate the host. MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData and MaximumObjectGraphDepth do not apply because the crash is not object-graph recursion. The CWE-789 fix is to reject non-{4,8,12} lengths before any insufficient-buffer handling so the slow path never stack-allocates from an untrusted body length.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Anyquery server mode binds a MySQL-wire TCP listener and forwards client SQL to the backing SQLite connection with no SQLITE_ATTACH authorizer. SQLite ATTACH DATABASE (and VACUUM INTO, which SQLite implements as attach) creates or overwrites a file at an attacker-chosen path. The Vitess/MySQL rewriter treats ATTACH as unparsable MySQL and, on StmtUnknown, runs the original statement against SQLite. Default auth is AuthServerNone when AuthFile/Users are empty, so an unauthenticated mysql client can write arbitrary files (cron, webroot PHP, authorized_keys) wherever the process can write, enabling AFW and environment-dependent RCE. Affected through 0.4.4; 0.4.5 installs a sandbox authorizer that denies non-memory ATTACH unless --allow-attach plus allowed dirs.

round11_research.bug_semantics: MessagePack skip-entire-structure walks nested arrays and maps by recursion and never increments MessagePackReader.Depth or consults MessagePackSecurity.MaximumObjectGraphDepth. In the 2.x/3.x API this is MessagePackReader.TrySkip(): maps/arrays call TrySkipNextMap/TrySkipNextArray, which loop TrySkip() on each child, so a skipped unknown field whose value is a chain of single-element fixarrays/fixmaps grows C# stack frames until an uncatchable StackOverflowException kills the process. Generated/dynamic formatters, IgnoreFormatter, and unknown-key/default branches invoke reader.Skip() during ordinary deserialization of untrusted payloads; UntrustedData does not mitigate because skip does not participate in depth accounting. The same recursion existed earlier as MessagePackBinary.ReadNextBlock (v1 formatters used that to skip unknown members).

round11_research.bug_semantics: GuardDog's programmatic remote project scanner (`ProjectScanner.scan_remote` / `PypiRequirementsScanner.scan_remote`) takes a caller-supplied repository URL, rewrites it with the blind substring `url.replace("github", "raw.githubusercontent")`, concatenates `/{branch}/{requirements_name}`, and then `requests.get`s that URL with HTTP Basic auth from `GIT_USERNAME`/`GH_TOKEN`. The rewrite never parses hostname, userinfo, or port, so a crafted URL such as `http://github@127.0.0.1:18081/owner/repo` becomes `http://raw.githubusercontent@127.0.0.1:18081/owner/repo/main/requirements.txt`. Requests treats that as a request to `127.0.0.1:18081` and attaches the GitHub PAT, yielding SSRF plus `GH_TOKEN` exfiltration (CWE-918).
