round11_research.bug_semantics: Authorino's AuthConfig spec.callbacks (originally spec.notify) is an unbounded collection of HTTP endpoints executed concurrently as phase 5 of every auth pipeline, after identity, metadata, authorization, and response. A developer-persona actor who can create or edit an AuthConfig, or a Kuadrant AuthPolicy that compiles into one, can attach arbitrarily many HTTP callbacks. Each Check request then fans out one goroutine and one outbound HTTP call per callback with no CRD maxItems/maxProperties, no controller count cap, and no executor throttle, so a single Authorino instance can be DoS'd while processing post-authorization callbacks (CWE-770/CWE-400).

round11_research.bug_semantics: GuardDog's default human-readable scan output concatenates attacker-controlled package identifiers, finding messages, file locations, and matched code snippets into the terminal without stripping or escaping C0/C1 control characters (including ESC). JSON/SARIF reporters are out of scope; the injection is the unsanitized human-readable sink (CWE-116). round11_research.bug_semantics: find-my-way lookup() forwards unsanitized req.method into find(), which does currentNode = this.trees[method] on a prototype-bearing object (this.trees = {}). Inherited keys such as constructor, toString, and __proto__ therefore resolve to Object.prototype properties instead of undefined. The truthy/undefined checks do not reject those values, so find() treats Function or Object.prototype as a radix node and throws when reading currentNode.prefix.length (originally split as prefix = currentNode.prefix; prefixLen = prefix.length). HTTP/2 is the remote trigger because Node's HTTP/2 :method is not restricted to http.METHODS the way HTTP/1 is. Route registration (on/off) does assert http.METHODS, but the request path never did.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-47219 cveMetadata.state=PUBLISHED (not rejected/withdrawn); CNA GitHub_M; GHSA-c96f-x56v-gq3h withdrawn_at=null. round11_research.bug_semantics: in_s3 downloads an S3 object and fully materializes the decompressed payload in memory before parsing. Default store_as is gzip; GzipExtractor.extract wraps the object body in Zlib::GzipReader and calls gz.read with no decompressed-size cap (later rewritten to loop concatenated members, still unbounded parts << gz.read / parts.join). gzip_command/lzma2/lzo extractors do the same via Open3.capture2 of gzip/xz/lzop -dc, returning the entire stdout. An attacker who can PUT a highly compressed object into the watched bucket can force Fluentd to expand a small blob into an arbitrarily large string, OOM-kill the process, and stop log collection on the node (CWE-770).

round11_research.bug_semantics: CWE-770 HTTP/2 connection-window starvation: when a stream's response body outruns the connection send window (default 65,535 bytes, shared across streams), Bandit.HTTP2.Connection queues the remaining bytes plus a reply closure in pending_sends and the stream/Plug process blocks forever inside GenServer.call(..., :infinity) to the connection process. The queue drains only on connection-level WINDOW_UPDATE/SETTINGS; nothing bounds the wait and nothing purges the queue. A client RST_STREAM is delivered to the blocked stream's mailbox but is never read while stuck in the call, so cancel frees nothing; periodic PINGs keep the transport read timeout from firing. Each stalled stream pins its process, Plug state, and any resource held across the write (e.g. a pooled upstream connection). Stream-window waits were later bounded at 15s; the connection-window path was not. Affects bandit 0.3.4 through 1.12.4.

round11_research.bug_semantics: asbplayer loads user-supplied subtitle files and, when the SubtitleHtml.render setting is on, leaves markup in cue text. SubtitleReader._filterText only optionally calls _decodeHTML (innerHTML-then-textContent strip) when subtitleHtml===remove; it performed no sanitization on the render path. Cue text is then interpolated unescaped into the video overlay via subtitle-controller._buildTextHtml → element-overlay innerHTML, and into the subtitle list via React dangerouslySetInnerHTML. A crafted .srt with HTML such as <script><button onmouseover=...> is therefore executed in the hosting streaming-site origin after the user loads the file with render-HTML enabled. Default remains SubtitleHtml.remove, so the setting is part of the UI:R path. round11_research.bug_semantics: The Flint/direct-query dispatcher classifies CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW as a Flint extension statement and forwards the whole string to Apache Spark without validating the inner SQL. The Flint grammar captures that inner query as an opaque token sequence (materializedViewQuery : .+?), so prohibited Spark SQL (TRANSFORM ... USING 'cmd', reflect/java System calls, CREATE FUNCTION, and other grammar-deny-list elements) that is blocked on the ordinary SQL path still executes on Spark workers. A remote authenticated user with async/direct-query access can therefore RCE by wrapping the payload in CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW ... AS <denied SQL>.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated stored XSS via utm_campaign in WP Statistics visitor/referral admin reports. An attacker POSTs to the public REST route /wp-statistics/v2/hit using the request signature that Helper::getHitsDefaultParams() localizes onto the public homepage. The required page_uri POST body is base64 and is applied by Hits::set_page_uri() and Helper::getRequestUri(), which decode it without sanitize_url() and therefore override the already-sanitized REQUEST_URI. Pages::get_page_type() always includes a search_query key, so sanitize_page_uri() never strips the query string; FilterQueryStringUrl() then keeps utm_campaign because it is on the default allow-list. The stored pages.uri query is later extracted by Url::getParam() into campaign labels and page-query tooltips (class wps-tooltip). Those titles use esc_attr/esc_html, but admin tooltipster is initialized with contentAsHTML:true, so the browser-decoded title is inserted as HTML when an administrator opens Visitors or Referred Visitors. Injection-pattern checks on the hit request block

round11_research.bug_semantics: ZeroBrew's Ruby formula compatibility shim downloaded secondary formula resources and URL-based patches with curl and then extracted or applied them during `zb install --build-from-source` without ever comparing the bytes to the sha256 values the formula DSL had already parsed. round11_research.bug_semantics: RNP 0.18.0 public-key encryption emits PKESK packets whose content-encryption key (CEK) is an all-zero byte array. init_encrypted_dst() allocates rnp::secure_bytes enckey(keylen, 0) and then calls encrypted_build_skesk() to generate the CEK and any SKESK packets. encrypted_build_skesk() returns true immediately when ctx.passwords is empty (the PKESK-only path) without calling ctx.sec_ctx.rng.get, so the zeroed buffer is encrypted to each recipient. Passphrase-based SKESK encryption still randomizes the CEK (or derives it from the password in the v4 single-password case) and is not affected.

round11_research.bug_semantics: MoneyPrinterTurbo mounts V1 video routes at prefix /api/v1. download_video is GET /download/{file_path:path} and therefore reachable as /api/v1/download/<file_path>. The handler takes the raw URL path parameter and builds video_path = os.path.join(utils.task_dir(), file_path) with no confinement, then returns FileResponse(path=video_path). round11_research.bug_semantics: Yggdrasil exports com.redhat.Yggdrasil1.Dispatch() on the system bus and forwards the caller's directive, message id, metadata, and payload to a named worker (including package-manager workers that can add repos and install/remove RPMs). A local unprivileged user could therefore force a privileged worker to install arbitrary packages, yielding LPE (CWE-280).

round11_research.bug_semantics: In seven OSPF Traffic Engineering / Segment Routing TLV parsers, a uint16_t loop accumulator (sum/len) is incremented by TLV_SIZE(), which is a uint32_t (TLV_HDR_SIZE + ROUNDUP(ntohs(tlvh->length), 4)). A crafted sub-TLV length near 0xffff makes TLV_SIZE() >= 65536; the add truncates/wraps so `sum < length` never becomes false while the for-increment still does tlvh = TLV_HDR_NEXT(tlvh) and walks off the LSA buffer. An adjacent OSPF peer can trigger that path with a Type 10/11 Opaque LS Update and crash ospfd (CWE-190 then CWE-125).
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-28532 state=PUBLISHED (cveMetadata.datePublished=2026-04-30, dateUpdated=2026-05-25); CNA VulnCheck; not rejected/withdrawn. GHSA-wjc3-2qjv-c8fp withdrawn_at=null. Affected FRRouting frr < 10.5.3.

Advisory mechanism: uint16_t accumulator truncates uint32_t TLV_SIZE() in seven OSPF TE/SR TLV parsers; crafted Type 10/11 Opaque LSA after OSPF adjacency causes OOB reads/crash. Finder credit: Kazuma Matsumoto (GMO Cybersecurity by IERAE).

round11_research.bug_semantics: CVE-2026-16336/GHSA-rf2w-6p6m-3cqv claim CWE-601 open redirect by manipulating a redirect_uri argument in core/trino-main/src/main/java/io/trino/server/ExternalUriInfo.java. That argument does not exist: ExternalUriInfo only reads UriInfo plus optional X-Forwarded-Prefix and rewrites the path of the same-origin request URI. Trino OAuth endpoints have no client-supplied redirect_uri/callback query parameter. startOAuth2Challenge issues HTTP 303 to the configured identity-provider authorization URI (NimbusOAuth2Client.createAuthorizationRequest); the OAuth redirect_uri query string on that IdP URL is server-constructed from the request base URI (Web UI: request.getUriInfo().getBaseUri().resolve("/oauth2/callback"); CLI/token exchange: externalUriInfo.absolutePath("/oauth2/callback")). Authorization-code theft as described in issue 29754 additionally requires the IdP to accept an unregistered redirect_uri, which RFC 6749 forbids and which Trino docs require operators to register as the exact coordinator callback.

round11_research.bug_semantics: A signed user TA can set TA_FLAG_CONCURRENT in its ta_head.flags even though that flag is documented as pseudo-TA only. The user-TA loader accepts any bits in TA_FLAGS_MASK and copies them onto the shared tee_ta_ctx. tee_ta_try_set_busy() then returns immediately without taking the busy lock, so two sessions of a single-instance multi-session user TA run concurrently on one context. Both sessions map and unmap memref parameters against the same uctx->vm_info.regions list with no lock, corrupting the list and freeing vm_region nodes still in use: a use-after-free in S-EL1.

PR/commit text: flag sits inside TA_FLAGS_MASK so a user TA can set it; tee_ta_try_set_busy() skips serialization; concurrent memref map/unmap corrupts uctx->vm_info.regions and frees live vm_region nodes.

That commit is not the BIC: at its parent and until 387b0ee39, ta_load() still used optional_flags = USER_MODE|EXEC_DDR|SINGLE_INSTANCE|MULTI_SESSION|SECURE_DATA_PATH|INSTANCE_KEEP_ALIVE|CACHE_MAINTENANCE, so (ta_head->flags & optional_flags) != ta_head->flags rejected CONCURRENT for user TAs.

GENMASK_32(h,l) is inclusive; GENMASK_32(8,2) includes bit 8 (TA_FLAG_CONCURRENT). Single parent, not a merge. git log -S TA_FLAGS_MASK -- lib/libutee/include/user_ta_header.h starts at this commit.

Immediate parent therefore cannot accept a user TA with the concurrent bit. At the BIC, skip-lock already existed in tee_ta_manager.c and utc->vm_info->regions / tee_mmu_map_param already existed, so the UAF race is reachable as soon as the mask allows the flag.

round11_research.bug_semantics: bgp_flowspec_op_decode() in bgpd/bgp_flowspec_util.c walks a chained FlowSpec numeric-operator NLRI and, on BGP_FLOWSPEC_CONVERT_TO_NON_OPAQUE, writes each decoded operator into a caller-supplied struct bgp_pbr_match_val array sized BGP_PBR_MATCH_VAL_MAX (5) via mval++. round11_research.bug_semantics: In bgp_attr_nhc(), a crafted BGP UPDATE carrying a Next Hop Dependent Characteristics (NHC) attribute can underflow the remaining-length counter. Remaining NHC length is a uint16 bgp_size_t. The TLV loop reads the 4-byte TLV header (code+length = BGP_NHC_TLV_MIN_LEN) then checks only `if (length < tlv_length)` before later doing `length -= tlv_length + BGP_NHC_TLV_MIN_LEN`. When remaining length is in [tlv_length, tlv_length+3], the check passes and the unsigned subtract wraps (e.g. 5-6 -> 65535). The loop is `while (length && STREAM_READABLE(s) >= BGP_NHC_TLV_MIN_LEN)`, and STREAM_READABLE is the whole UPDATE stream, so a wrapped length keeps parsing subsequent UPDATE bytes as NHC TLVs (allocations/DoS). STREAM_READABLE < tlv_length can stop an over-read of the stream itself, but does not stop the underflow. CWE-191; unauthenticated remote DoS via BGP UPDATE.

round11_research.bug_semantics: rfapiRibBi2Ri() in bgpd/rfapi/rfapi_rib.c copies a BGP path's VNC sub-TLVs into struct rfapi_info. For BGP_VNC_SUBTLV_TYPE_RFPOPTION it treats pEncap->value[0]/value[1] as an inner type/length and XCALLOC/memcpy's pEncap->length-2 bytes with no check that the sub-TLV is long enough. bgp_attr_encap() will store a VNC sub-TLV of any sublength (including 0/1/2) from a BGP UPDATE; ENABLE_BGP_VNC is on unless --disable-bgp-vnc. A short RFPOPTION then OOBs on value[] (flexible array sized to sublength) and computes length-2 as a negative int (uint16_t promotes) that XCALLOC takes as a huge size_t, or XCALLOC(0) when length==2. Callers rfapiRibPreloadBi/rfapiRibUpdatePendingNode run this on imported VPN/VNC routes, crashing or exhausting bgpd (DoS).

CVE-2025-24928: xmlSnprintfElements (valid.c) formats DTD validation error text into a fixed stack buffer; the remaining-size check counted the QName prefix and local name separately and did not account for prefix+':' +name together, so a ~3kb QName prefix overflows the stack while reporting a validation error (CWE-787/CWE-121). CVE-2024-56171: xmlSchemaIDCFillNodeTables and xmlSchemaBubbleIDCNodeTables (xmlschemas.c) keep a stale items pointer after xmlSchemaItemListAdd reallocates the identity-constraint duplicate list, a use-after-free on crafted XSD (xsd:keyref plus recursive types with extra identity constraints) or on untrusted instance documents validated against such schemas. Attackers supply malicious DTD/XSD (or documents that trigger DTDVALID) to DoS or potentially execute code. Nokogiri does not reimplement these C functions; it downloads and compiles the pinned libxml2 tarball.

round11_research.bug_semantics: A remote unauthenticated ForwardOpen can supply a mixed-class CIP application path (Assembly as path1 plus a non-Assembly endpoint such as Identity instance 1 or Ethernet Link). check_path()/ResolveInstances() accept any existing class+instance and bind those objects as consuming/producing I/O endpoints; class 0/1 handling does not require kCipAssemblyClass. CipConnMgrClass::forward_open then dispatches via mgmnt_class (path1 Assembly) into CipAssemblyClass::OpenConnection -> OpenIO -> ConnectionData::CorrectSizes, which forces attribute 3 and casts instance data to ByteBuf*/CipByteArray. Identity attribute 3 is uint16_t product_code_ and Ethernet Link attribute 3 is a 6-byte MAC, so ByteBuf::size() (limit-start) reads off the true object (ASan global-buffer-overflow on product_code_, heap-buffer-overflow on physical_address) and aborts the POSIX sample server.

round11_research.bug_semantics: CVE-2025-71346 is a downstream packaging of libxml2 CVE-2025-32415. Nokogiri CRuby vendors libxml2 and exposes XML Schema validation (Nokogiri::XML::Schema → xmlSchemaParse / xmlSchemaValidateDoc / xmlSchemaValidateFile). In libxml2 before 2.13.8 (and 2.14.0–2.14.1), xmlSchemaIDCFillNodeTables in xmlschemas.c copies bind->nbNodes into a local nbNodeTable and later iterates with that stale count after the identity-constraint node table can shrink, causing a heap buffer under-read (CWE-125). The path is reachable when validating an untrusted XSD, or when validating an untrusted document against a trusted schema that uses xsd:keyref together with recursively defined types that have additional identity constraints. Upstream/MITRE rate it 2.9 LOW; impact is availability (crash/DoS), not a Nokogiri-authored memory bug. JRuby is off this libxml2 path; CRuby built against a patched system libxml2 is also unaffected.

round11_research.bug_semantics: CIPster's generic attribute encode/decode treats a kCipByteArray and a companion kCipByteArrayLength as views over the same ByteBuf, which stores only start/limit and derives size() as limit-start with no immutable backing-store capacity. A remote SetAttributeSingle on a writable kCipByteArrayLength reaches CipAttribute::SetAttrData -> DecodeData(kCipByteArrayLength), which rebuilds the shared ByteBuf as ByteBuf(bb->data(), aBuf.get16()) from an attacker-supplied uint16 and thereby poisons limit. A subsequent GetAttributeSingle on the aliased kCipByteArray (GetAttrData -> EncodeData) over-reads the real allocation, and a subsequent SetAttributeSingle (SetAttrData -> DecodeData(kCipByteArray)) constructs a BufWriter from the inflated end() and memcpy-writes past the backing buffer. Stock Assembly instance attr 4 registers kCipByteArrayLength as gettable-only (isSetableSingle default false), so the default sample is not the demonstrated path; the public AttributeInsert API can register both types writable against one ByteBuf, which is the confirmed API-enabled attack.

round11_research.bug_semantics: CIPster's generic AttributeInsert(CipDataType, void*) binds an untyped storage cookie to an arbitrary CIP type with no layout check. An API-enabled deployment can register the same ByteBuf object as both a writable kCipByteArray and a writable kCipUdint. A remote unauthenticated EtherNet/IP SetAttributeSingle on the UDINT view hits DecodeData(kCipUdint), which stores 32 bits into ByteBuf.start (the first pointer of {start, limit}) while leaving limit unchanged, inflating logical size. A following GetAttributeSingle or SetAttributeSingle on the byte-array view hits EncodeData/DecodeData(kCipByteArray), which construct BufReader/BufWriter from that poisoned ByteBuf; BufWriter::append then memcpy's against attacker-controlled start/limit (ASan: 80-byte OOB read/write from backing-16). The default sample is not claimed exploitable; the primitive is CIPster's public attribute-registration API plus generic Get/SetAttrData.

round11_research.bug_semantics: GET /a/share/link/{Uuid} (SharesHandler.GetShareLink in idm/share/rest/handler.go) returns the full ShareLink object for a workspace UUID with no READ authorization. The handler reads the path UUID, calls LinkById, and writes the result. LinkById reaches GetLinkWorkspace, which calls GetOrCreateWorkspace with a nil owner and SearchWorkspace carrying only a WorkspaceSingleQuery and no ResourcePolicyQuery; PrepareResourcePolicyQuery returns that query unmodified when ResourcePolicyQuery is nil, so the workspace service applies no policy filter. Sibling GET /a/share/cell/{Uuid} (GetCell) loads the workspace then requires MatchPolicies(..., ResourcePolicyAction_READ) and returns CellNotFound so existence is not disclosed. The UUID is not secret: the unauthenticated /public/{hash} minisite embeds it as START_REPOSITORY. Any standard-role account can therefore recover LinkHash and LinkUrl, the owner's user identifier, the hidden share-user login, permissions, download limit and count, target users, expiry, and PasswordRequired, while a direct read of the shared node by the same account is refused (CWE-862).
evidence: CVE.org record https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-76032 is state=PUBLISHED (CNA VulnCheck, not withdrawn/rejected); GHSA-v2c6-62qq-rjcr withdrawn_at=null. round11_research.bug_semantics: CipAppPath::deserialize_symbolic trusts a symbolic-segment header's self-declared length and copies that many bytes from the current input pointer without checking remaining readable size. CipMessageRouterRequest::DeserializeMRReq (and historically InitRequest) only validates the outer path word-count (path_size = word_count*2) and then hands a 2-byte BufReader/limit to the app-path parser. A remote unconnected SendRRData Message Router request with body 0e 01 7f 41 therefore passes the outer check (path word count 1 → 2 path bytes 7f 41) while first=0x7f yields symbol_size=31; after consuming the header only 1 byte remains and memcpy/pointer-walk reads past the path window into/beyond the global TCP receive buffer s_buf. The same unbounded copy exists on the ANSI Extended Symbol branch. Demonstrated impact is a remotely triggerable out-of-bounds read / ASan global-buffer-overflow DoS on the official POSIX sample (CWE-125/CWE-119).

round11_research.bug_semantics: SAML 2.0 HTTP-Redirect binding payloads (login SAMLResponse or logout SAMLRequest) are Base64-decoded then inflated through java.util.zip.InflaterOutputStream into an unbounded ByteArrayOutputStream. An unauthenticated attacker can send a small DEFLATE bomb on a GET to the ACS or SLO endpoint; the inflater writes without a size cap and can exhaust heap (CWE-400 DoS). POST binding skips inflate and is not this bug. The 2026 fix wraps the writer in CappedOutputStream (1 MiB) and, for login, also recommends OpenSaml5AuthenticationTokenConverter#setShouldConvertGetRequests(false).

round11_research.bug_semantics: Outbound HTTP/1.1 start-line fields are serialized to the wire without neutralizing CR/LF or other illegal bytes. HTTPRequestEncoder writes HTTPRequestHead.uri and HTTPMethod.RAW verbatim into the request line; HTTPResponseEncoder writes a custom HTTPResponseStatus.reasonPhrase verbatim into the status line. An attacker who can influence those fields (proxy-forwarded URL/method, client redirect to a crafted URL, or a custom reason phrase) injects a second request or response on the same connection (request smuggling / response splitting, CWE-93). From 2.42.0 the default NIOHTTPRequestHeadersValidator / NIOHTTPResponseHeadersValidator (enableOutboundHeaderValidation=true on addHTTPClientHandlers / addHTTPServerHandlers) only gated header names and values via areValidToSend, so a CRLF URI/method/reason still reached the encoder.
evidence: GHSA-cq87-8r7h-962v (withdrawn_at=null; published 2026-05-21 by Lukasa): CRLF injection in outbound HTTP request URI/method/response reason phrase via NIOHTTPRequestHeadersValidator/NIOHTTPResponseHeadersValidator; affected >=2.0.0 <=2.99.0; patched 2.100.0. round11_research.bug_semantics: NIOHTTP1's HTTPDecoder accumulates every HTTP/1 header field into an unbounded [(String,String)] (then HTTPHeaders) before any application handler runs. After the llhttp switch the decoder enforced only an 80 KB cap on a single field name/value (currentFieldByteLength, reset in finish() per field). There was no running total of header-block bytes and no field-count cap, so a remote peer could send hundreds of thousands of small valid headers on one request/response and exhaust memory (or crash consumers that bridge into swift-http-types HTTPFields). Attack path: unauthenticated HTTP/1 bytes -> BetterHTTPParser on_header_field/on_header_value -> HTTPDecoder.didReceiveHeaderValue headers.append -> HTTPServerRequestPart.head / HTTPClientResponsePart.head. Fixed in 2.100.0 by NIOHTTPDecoderLimitConfiguration (maxHeaderFieldSize 80 KB, maxHeaderListSize 2 MB, maxHeaderFieldCount 256) rejecting overflow with HTTPParserError.headerOverflow.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Apache Neethi policy normalization (Policy.normalize -> AbstractPolicyOperator.normalizeOperator) resolves wsp:PolicyReference children by registry lookup and then recursively normalizes the referenced Policy's components with no cycle set. A WS-Policy graph where Policy A references Policy B and B references A therefore re-enters normalizeOperator on the same policies until StackOverflowError or an unbounded hang. The pre-3.2.2 TYPE_POLICY_REF branch (3.2.1 AbstractPolicyOperator.java:128-148) looks up the URI, wraps the resolved Policy's children in All, and calls normalizeOperator again; PolicyReference.normalize is only an entry point into that same operator path. Attackers supply or register such a circular document and trigger normalize(true), causing DoS (CWE-400). Patched in 3.2.2 by tracking resolving policy ids and throwing RuntimeException on a repeat.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Flask-Security-Too 5.8.0 OAuth reauthentication (verify) treats any datastore-resolved OAuth user as proof that the current session may be marked fresh. oauth_verify_response() calls _oauth_response_common(), then on a truthy user writes session['fs_paa']=time.time() with no check that that user is current_user. An attacker who already holds a stale authenticated victim session can start OAuth verify and complete the provider callback with a different account (attacker@example.com). The session identity stays the victim, but freshness is reset, so freshness-gated account actions (reproduced on built-in /change-username) succeed. oauthresponse() login is out of scope: it logs in as the OAuth user rather than minting freshness for a different session principal.

round11_research.bug_semantics: In Basic Authentication, check_request in src/basic_auth.rs returns 401 immediately when the supplied username does not equal the configured userid, and only then calls bcrypt::verify on the password. round11_research.bug_semantics: CWE-502 Java deserialization RCE in the deprecated fabric-sdk-java client. HFClient.deSerializeChannel(byte[]) / deSerializeChannel(File) wrap caller-supplied bytes in a raw ObjectInputStream and call readObject() with no ObjectInputFilter. Channel was made Serializable in the same change and implements a private readObject() that only defaultReadObject()s and rehydrates transients; that hook is not the entry point. Channel bytes are not sent by Fabric peers; this is a client-side sink. The GHSA snippet misplaces deSerializeChannel on Channel.java; the live method is on HFClient.java.

round11_research.bug_semantics: DaoAuthenticationProvider equalizes username-existence timing by running PasswordEncoder against a dummy hash when UserDetailsService throws UsernameNotFoundException. AbstractUserDetailsAuthenticationProvider.authenticate() still invokes DefaultPreAuthenticationChecks (UserDetails.isAccountNonLocked/isEnabled/isAccountNonExpired) before additionalAuthenticationChecks (the real passwordEncoder.matches). If a found user is locked, disabled, or account-expired, the pre-check throws and the expensive password comparison is skipped. An unauthenticated attacker can therefore distinguish those account attributes from both unknown usernames (dummy encode/match) and enabled accounts (real match) via response time (CWE-208).

round11_research.bug_semantics: ByteBuffer stores reader/writer indices and capacity as UInt32. The Int-to-UInt32 helpers (_toIndex/_toCapacity, originally toIndex/toCapacity) converted with a truncating initializer, which on 64-bit platforms silently discarded the high 32 bits instead of trapping. Safety preconditions then observed the already-truncated value, so an attacker-influenced Int > UInt32.max (for example 0x100000000) became 0 and passed checks. copyBytes(at:to:length:) reserved/copied using the truncated destination index while ptr.dropFirst(toIndex) still used the original Int, producing an out-of-bounds write. writeWithUnsafeMutableBytes(minimumWritableBytes:) reserved via _toCapacity, so a crafted request larger than UInt32.max yielded a pointer whose length did not match the requested size and could be overflowed on the subsequent write. moveReaderIndex/moveWriterIndex(forwardBy:) and ByteBuffer(takingOwnershipOf:allocator:) wrap logically but do not expose wild pointers. Fixed by switching the helpers to trapping UInt32(_:), leaving truncatingIfNeeded only in getSlice after Int-domain bounds checks.

round11_research.bug_semantics: CWE-863 cross-organization authorization bypass on HTTP filestore GET. round11_research.bug_semantics: SubjectX500PrincipalExtractor turns an X.509 client certificate's X500Principal into an RFC2253 (CN) or RFC1779 (email OID) DN string and takes matcher.find() group(1) from the regex CN=(.*?)(?:,|$) or OID.1.2.840.113549.1.9.1=(.*?)(?:,|$). Because the regex is unanchored and stops at the first CN=/OID= substring, a CN or OU value that embeds a second DN-like fragment (for example OU=CN=duke,) is parsed as that other username. A crafted client certificate can therefore impersonate another user in X.509 pre-authentication. The vendor advisory and CVE.org record keep this as a real published issue affecting Spring Security 7.0.0–7.0.4 (CWE-297); exploitation assumes the cert already passed a trusted upstream.

round11_research.bug_semantics: CWE-639 IDOR on Askbot avatar mutation views. `admin_or_owner_required` in askbot/views/avatar_views.py is supposed to allow only an administrator or the profile owner, but two interacting mistakes let any authenticated user change another user's avatar: (1) it compared `request.user.id` (int) to the Django URL capture `user_id` (always a string from `^avatar/upload/(?P<user_id>\d+)/$` and sibling routes), so the owner check never succeeded in Python 2 or 3; (2) when that check failed it fell through to `login_required(func)(request, user_id)`, which only tests authentication and then still invokes the view. A logged-in attacker POSTs to `/avatar/upload/<victim_id>/` (or intercepts and rewrites user_id) and replaces the victim's profile picture. round11_research.bug_semantics: Velociraptor's server-side VQL query() plugin (vql/tools/query.go QueryPlugin.Call) accepts org_id to evaluate a subquery in another org. The plugin builds the subquery scope with ScopeBuilderFromScope(scope), which copies the caller's ACLManager (the current org's ACL token), then on org_id only replaces builder.Config with org_manager.GetOrgConfig(arg.OrgId). round11_research.bug_semantics: The interactive OIDC/OAuth authorization-code flow generates a random CSRF `state`, includes it on the authorization request, then accepts the IdP callback's `code` without comparing the returned `state` to the session value. round11_research.bug_semantics: Apache Neethi policy normalization converts nested All/ExactlyOne (historically And/Xor) operators into DNF by taking an unbounded Cartesian cross-product of child alternatives. round11_research.bug_semantics: music-metadata's ASF Header Extension walker parseExtensionObject() reads a 24-byte sub-object header, then treats header.objectSize as both the payload-skip length (objectSize - 24) and the loop decrement. When a crafted sub-object has objectSize=0, remaining is -24; tokenizer.ignore(-24) on the Padding/Compatibility/Index-Placeholder paths rewinds FileTokenizer/BufferTokenizer by 24 bytes, extensionSize -= 0 never shrinks, and the same header is re-read forever (CWE-835 hang/DoS). parseStream() is not affected because ReadStreamTokenizer.ignore() rejects the negative skip. HeaderObjectToken.len is 24.

round11_research.bug_semantics: soup_message_headers_set_content_disposition() concatenates a caller-controlled disposition type and params (for example filename) in set_content_foo() and stores the result as Content-Disposition. round11_research.bug_semantics: SoupServer multi-range handling sorts SoupRange entries with sort_ranges() in soup-message-headers.c, then merges overlapping ranges. The comparator subtracts two goffset (gint64) start values and returns that difference as int. When requested start offsets differ by more than INT_MAX (~2.1e9), truncation flips the comparison sign, violating qsort's ordering contract. The subsequent merge then treats mis-ordered non-overlapping ranges as overlapping and silently drops requested spans from HTTP 206 Partial Content responses on bodies larger than about 2 GB, with no error status.

round11_research.bug_semantics: When pam_winbind mkhomedir is enabled, _pam_mkhomedir() takes the target account's pw_dir from getpwnam() and, after _pam_create_homedir() treats an already-existing path as success, _pam_chown_homedir() chowns that path with no check that it is not a critical system directory. Accounts whose home is '/' (a common default for nobody and other system accounts) therefore have '/' reowned when a PAM session is opened as that account — by root su or by a non-root user with a narrow sudo run-as-that-account grant — breaking sshd StrictModes, sudo, and package-manager ownership checks. On RHEL '/' ships mode 0555, so the impact is availability loss rather than write privilege escalation.
evidence: CVE.org record CVE-2026-15779 is state=PUBLISHED (CNA Red Hat, datePublished 2026-07-15); not rejected/withdrawn. GHSA-6fmw-7w5g-3pf9 withdrawn_at is null.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Exported helper setNestedValue (source src/util/object.ts; published as lib/util/object.js) takes a caller-supplied dot-separated path, splits it on '.', and forwards the key array to @antv/util set with no filtering of __proto__, prototype, or constructor. That setter walks keys and does o[key] = value; for a plain target, path __proto__.polluted resolves o to Object.prototype and writes an inherited property, and constructor.prototype.polluted does the same via Function.prototype. Because src/index.ts re-exports src/util (which re-exports object.ts), any consumer that passes untrusted path strings into the public API can pollute Object.prototype (CWE-1321). The CWE-94 label is secondary misclassification of the same sink. Attack is not a built-in remote RCE; it requires the application to feed attacker-controlled path/value into the exported helper.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Reflected XSS (CWE-79) in YaCyDefaultServlet.sendDirectory(): when dirAllowed directory listing is served, listing HTML is built with resource.getListHTML(base, ...). round11_research.bug_semantics: js_typed_array_sort with a user comparator sorts an index array, then rebuilds the typed array by reading array_tmp[array_idx[i]] without bounding j against the post-sort length. A comparator can shrink a resizable ArrayBuffer after large indices have already been moved to valid slots, so js_TA_cmp_generic's a_idx/b_idx >= count check never fires for those entries. After rqsort the function does len = min_int(len, p->u.array.count) and js_malloc(len * elt_size) for array_tmp, then copies with unbounded j, producing a heap-buffer-overflow read of the shrunken tmp (ASAN: 10-byte allocation from js_typed_array_sort when newSz=10 and leftover index 255).

round11_research.bug_semantics: js_atomics_store and js_atomics_op (and the other Atomics ops that share that pointer-cache pattern) call js_atomics_get_ptr, which returns a raw pointer into a TypedArray's ArrayBuffer. They then convert argv[2] with JS_ToIntegerFree / JS_ToUint32 / JS_ToBigInt*, which can run attacker-controlled JS via valueOf. That JS can rab.resize() a resizable ArrayBuffer; js_array_buffer_resize js_realloc()s the backing store (freeing the old allocation) and updates TypedArray views, but does not set abuf->detached. After conversion the atomics code only re-checks abuf->detached, then performs atomic_store / atomic_fetch_* on the stale pointer — heap use-after-free. PoC: new ArrayBuffer(1024, {maxByteLength: ...}); Atomics.store/add(i32, 0, {valueOf(){ rab.resize(0); return 123; }}). Detach-during-conversion was already handled; resize-without-detach was not.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Default `agent-coderag sync <path>` always calls `CodeRAGManager.sync_dependencies()`. round11_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated CWE-918 SSRF with HTTP-error reflection in the OIDC token-exchange path. Exchange() takes the Authorization bearer JWT, reads the unverified iss claim via apiauth.ExtractIssuer, and immediately performs OIDC discovery against that string (originally oidc.NewProvider(ctx, issuer); later provider.Get → oidc.NewProvider). go-oidc GETs {iss}/.well-known/openid-configuration and follows redirects using the default HTTP client, so a crafted iss (http://internal-host, link-local metadata, attacker HTTPS that 302s internally) causes the server to fetch attacker-chosen URLs before any signature or trust-policy check. Discovery failures are wrapped into the gRPC error (go-oidc formats '%s: %s' with status and body), so internal response bodies can reflect to the caller; later logging of provider/token-exchange errors added a second leak. Affected <= v0.5.2; first patched v0.5.3.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Optional PKCE in handleAuthorizationCodeGrant can be skipped by a downgrade: parseAuthRequest stores code_challenge only if the authorization request includes it, and the token endpoint verifies a code_verifier only when the grant already has codeChallenge (isPkceEnabled = !!grantData.codeChallenge). round11_research.bug_semantics: OPA's HTTP Data API turns the request path into a Rego query by building an ast.Ref (stringPathToRef / stringPathToDataRef) and feeding ref.String() to rego.Query(), which re-parses the string. After d3f5102aa, non-identifier ref terms are emitted as [" + raw path segment + "] with no JSON escaping of quotes. A segment such as foo"];malicious_call();x=[" (URL-encoded foo%22%5D%3Bmalicious_call%28%29%3Bx%3D%5B%22) therefore serializes to a multi-statement query (data["foo"];malicious_call();x=[""]), injecting attacker-controlled Rego. Evaluation cannot exfiltrate arbitrary documents beyond the requested path, but the injected code can force success/failure (oracle / misdirected decisions) or be computationally expensive (DoS). v1.4.0 rejects quote characters in path terms and re-parses the constructed query, requiring a single ref.

round11_research.flaw_origin: The Data API has constructed evaluation queries from path.String() since 3ebbeede6ce37a3e6db6aac380ba762388121093 (2017), but that round-trip was safe while Ref.String() wrapped non-identifier terms with p.String() (strconv.Quote). d3f5102aa4d60a7f7b037761c5a43ac776359b56 (PR #7172, 2024-11-14) rewrote Ref.String() for allocation reduction and replaced "["+p.String()+"]" with unescaped ["+str+"], first writing the interpolation that lets HTTP path quotes break out of the reconstructed query. GHSA/CVE affected range < 1.4.0 is broader than the regression (BIC is first tagged in v1.0.0; v0.70.0 does not contain it).
round11_research.reasoning: CVE-2025-46569 / GHSA-6m8w-jc87-6cr7 is a real, published code-injection issue in the standalone OPA Data API: an HTTP path is turned into a Rego query and re-parsed, so a crafted path can inject extra statements. The attack surface lives in server makeRego (and the health-check path) calling rego.Query(stringPathToDataRef(urlPath).String()), but that pattern existed since 2017 and was a safe AST round-trip while Ref.String() used strconv.Quote for bracketed terms. round11_research.bug_semantics: Client-side heap OOB write in smb2_add_iovector(): it stores into v->iov[v->niov] and increments niov with no upper bound against the fixed array iov[SMB2_MAX_VECTORS] (256). On receive, a compound SMB2 response with NextCommand set keeps the same smb2->in vector set, appending header/fixed/variable/pad iovecs for each chained PDU and then, when is_chained, adding another header and looping via goto read_more_data without resetting niov. A malicious server can therefore drive niov past 256 and write adjacent heap. SMB2_OPLOCK_BREAK notifications with message_id 0xffffffffffffffff skip smb2_find_pdu(), so the chain need not match outstanding request IDs; that is an exploitability amplifier, not the overflow sink. Unauthenticated remote DoS / potential RCE against a libsmb2 client.

round11_research.bug_semantics: mailboxes/detachall.cgi saves each MIME attachment into a temp directory then zips the result. When an attachment has a filename, the CGI sets $fn from decode_mimewords($a->{'filename'}) and writes with open_tempfile(FILE, ">$temp/$fn", 0, 1). The fourth argument is $notemp=1, so web-lib-funcs.pl open_tempfile writes directly via Perl open(">$file") with no basename check; it only rejects CR/LF/NUL. An attacker-controlled Content-Disposition filename such as ../../etc/cron.d/pwn therefore escapes $temp and overwrites an arbitrary path as the Webmin process user (often root). Trigger is an authenticated Read User Mail user invoking detach-all on a crafted message (CVE-2026-49103: CWE-24, CVSS 9.4, PR:L, affected < 2.640).

round11_research.bug_semantics: module_34301.c (KeePass AESKDF / KDBX v4) tokenizes hash-line field 9 (header) with len_min=400 and len_max=600 hex characters, then hex_decode()s the token into keepass4->header[64] (256 bytes) with no size check. A maximal 600-hex token decodes to 300 bytes and writes 44 bytes past the header field; 8 of those bytes leave the 328-byte keepass4_t esalt into adjacent heap-chunk metadata, causing heap corruption or SIGSEGV when hashcat parses an attacker-supplied hash file.

round11_research.bug_semantics: The DuckDB AWS extension exposed SQL table function load_aws_credentials, which resolved the AWS default credential provider chain (profile files, env, IMDSv2, IRSA, ECS task role, EC2 instance role) and returned access_key_id, secret_access_key, session_token, and region as result columns. Named parameter redact_secret (default true) gated only the secret_access_key column; CALL load_aws_credentials(redact_secret=false) emitted the secret in plaintext. That opt-out was independent of DuckDB's later database-wide allow_unredacted_secrets=false policy (AllowUnredactedSecretsSetting), so any principal with SQL execution could dump live AWS credentials without enabling unredacted secrets. The original return path also always printed session_token unredacted. The complete fix deleted the function rather than relying on a bind-time policy check.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated CRLF injection into the system crontab via GET /crontab. Express decodes URL-encoded %0a/%0d in req.query.env_vars; app.js passes that string unsanitized to crontab.set_crontab, which prefixes the generated crontab file with `${envVars}\n` (originally `env_vars + "\n"`) and then execs `crontab <file>`. Lines after the injected newline are treated as extra cron records, so a caller can install arbitrary scheduled commands through a field intended only for crontab environment assignments (PATH, MAILTO, HOME). Basic auth is optional (BASIC_AUTH_USER/PWD); Docker images bind HOST=0.0.0.0:8000.

potential_fix.approach: Reject env_vars content that is not a crontab environment assignment: split on newlines, keep only optional comments and NAME=value lines, drop any line matching a cron schedule (five fields or @reboot/@daily/etc. plus a command). Do not write raw req.query.env_vars into the crontab file. Change GET /crontab to POST so query-string CRLF and CSRF-via-GET cannot install jobs. Keep auth optional only behind an explicit bind/auth warning; default Docker should not expose an unauthenticated crontab writer on 0.0.0.0.
potential_fix.rationale: The injectable primitive is extra crontab records created from decoded newlines in a parameter meant for env assignments. Accepting only KEY=value/comment lines closes the CWE-93 breakout; moving the install endpoint off GET removes the unauthenticated one-request install path described in the advisory.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated stored XSS on invoice/bill detail timelines. An authenticated user stores HTML/JavaScript in their profile name (PATCH profile/{user}; User request only validates name as required|string; UpdateUser persists raw input). When that user creates or cancels a document, Create.php/Restore.php copy owner->name into $user_name and the Blade views interpolate it unescaped into trans('documents.slider.create'|cancel) replacements such as ':user created this :type on :date'. The date field is already a trusted HTML <span>, so the composed description is passed with {!! trans(...) !!} into x-show.accordion.head, which emits {!! $description !!}. Laravel trans() does not HTML-escape replacements, so another viewer of the document executes the stored name as HTML/JS.

round11_research.bug_semantics: llama-server use-after-free of ctx_server.vocab on six HTTP tokenization-family endpoints (/tokenize, /detokenize, /infill, /apply-template, /rerank, /anthropic/count_tokens) when --sleep-idle-seconds is enabled. Those handlers construct server_res_generator, which calls wait_until_no_sleep() and then drops mutex_tasks; they then tokenize or otherwise dereference ctx_server.vocab on the HTTP worker thread, bypassing the completion task queue. Concurrently the main loop can observe an empty queue, enter sleep, and run destroy() -> llama_init.reset(), which frees llama_model (and the embedded llama_vocab) without nulling the cached vocab pointer. The TOCTOU window after the awake check lets a worker finish using a dangling vocab pointer, causing crash or potential code execution via heap reclaim.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-43632 is PUBLISHED (not rejected/withdrawn); CNA VulnCheck; datePublished 2026-08-06; affected ggml-org/llama.cpp b7492..b9060; CWE-416 and CWE-367. GHSA-3f2h-96vw-c84x withdrawn_at is null. Description matches tokenize-endpoint UAF, not unbounded task creation.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated staff using CiviCRM contact Search Builder (operator Regex) reach CRM_Contact_BAO_Query::buildClause with op=RLIKE. The RLIKE arm interpolates the user-supplied $value into CAST($field AS BINARY) RLIKE BINARY '$value' without CRM_Utils_Type::escape / CRM_Core_DAO::escapeString. Other operators in the same function take the default branch, which does escape. The operator is user-selectable via CRM_Core_SelectValues::getSearchBuilderOperators() ('RLIKE' => Regex) and is exercised by tests/phpunit/CRM/Contact/SelectorTest.php::testWhereClauseByOperator.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Akaunting's common BulkActions dispatcher takes a request-controlled handle and invokes it as a method on the resolved BulkAction class (for example App\BulkActions\Auth\Users). Authorization is supposed to come from the $actions metadata, but the 3.1.21 dispatcher only consults $actions[$handle]['permission'] when the submitted handle is a direct array key. That misses (1) modal submit handles such as update, declared under edit via 'handle' => 'update', and (2) callable methods such as destroy that exist on the class/base but are not action keys (delete is the keyed alias). An authenticated user with only read-admin-panel (default Manager) can POST /{company_id}/common/bulk-actions/auth/users with handle=update&roles[]=<admin> or handle=destroy and escalate or delete users, because UpdateUser/DeleteUser do not re-check update-auth-users/delete-auth-users.

round11_research.bug_semantics: llama.cpp DRY sampler stores caller-supplied dry_allowed_length as a signed int32 with no lower bound. An HTTP /v1/completions or /v1/chat/completions body can set dry_allowed_length to INT32_MIN; json_value copies that value into sampling params and llama_sampler_init_dry stores it unchanged. llama_sampler_dry_apply then (1) fails the last_n_repeat <= dry_allowed_length early-return because any token count is greater than INT32_MIN, (2) treats every repeat_len as eligible because repeat_len >= INT32_MIN is always true, and (3) computes int repeat_exp = repeat_len - dry_allowed_length, a signed integer underflow of INT32_MIN that is undefined in int32 and yields an out-of-range exponent used to mutate logits. Cyera/VulnCheck observed the resulting heap OOB read/underflow as SIGSEGV DoS or corrupted sampling probabilities. The same unbounded int is also accepted by --dry-allowed-length.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-43628 state=PUBLISHED (not rejected/withdrawn); CNA VulnCheck; GHSA-wvf4-v63v-mwm5 withdrawn_at=null. Affected ggml-org/llama.cpp b3978..b9058 and 0.11.0..0.17.1. Attack: HTTP dry_allowed_length=INT32_MIN on /v1/completions or /v1/chat/completions.

round11_research.bug_semantics: MiniServ treats any simplified request path matching the default unauth regex ^[A-Za-z0-9\-/_]+\.conf$ as pre-auth static content. handle_request does $simple =~ /$u/ over that allowlist and, on match, sets validated=4 and serves the file from the Webmin root with no session. Because the character class includes '/', an unauthenticated network client can GET any *.conf under module directories in the install root (not a single known public asset). CWE-185/CWE-777: the allowlist regex is incorrect and under-constrained for an authentication gate.

round11_research.bug_semantics: The IdentityServer profile page at /identity-server/account/profile is a cookie-authenticated UI that immediately commits email (and username) changes through DefaultUserService.UpdateAsync -> UserManager.SetEmailAsync with no confirmation step. The first-party PoC is not a token-less cross-site POST: an attacker uploads HTML as a Squidex asset and serves it inline on the same origin, then iframes the real profile form under a decoy overlay so the victim's click submits that form. Assets are delivered with Content-Disposition inline (unless download=1) and only Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'none', which blocks stored XSS but not iframe/CSS UI-redress. Profile POSTs carry [AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken] and @Html.AntiForgeryToken() (the 7.4.0 CSRF fix), and antiforgery emits X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN unless identity.suppressXFrameOptionsHeader is true; SAMEORIGIN does not stop a same-origin asset iframe, so the antiforgery cookie/token travel with the clickjacked submit. Durable impact is changing the victim's email without verification and pivoting account recovery. CVE.org remains PUBLISHED (CNA MITRE, CISA-ADP CWE-352); GHSA withdrawn_at is null.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-31016 state=PUBLISHED (not rejected/withdrawn), datePublished=2026-06-29; CISA-ADP CWE-352; GHSA-8hjx-7pv7-rr27 withdrawn_at=null, affected/patched versions unknown.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Webmin miniserv.pl authenticates SSL-client-certificate users by mapping a certificate DN through find_user_by_cert() and setting $validated=2. After trust_real_ip was reused as a proxy-header trust flag, a client-supplied X-SSL-Client-DN header was treated as that DN without a verified TLS client certificate from this connection. With proxy-IP trust enabled and at least one user bound to a client cert, an unauthenticated peer that reaches miniserv directly (not via the intended reverse proxy) can forge X-SSL-Client-DN and impersonate that user (CWE-290). round11_research.bug_semantics: fgetl() in src/filehandling.c treats line_sz as content capacity and then always writes a NUL at line_buf[line_len]. When an input line is exactly line_sz bytes, line_len equals the caller's allocation and the terminator is a one-byte heap write past the buffer (CWE-193/CWE-787). The CVE/GHSA PoC is a hash/potfile/wordlist line of exactly HCBUFSIZ_LARGE (16,777,216) bytes with no newline; callers such as hlfmt_detect (src/hlfmt.c), hashes_init_stage1 (src/hashes.c), potfile_read (src/potfile.c), and outfile_check (src/outfile_check.c) allocate hcmalloc(HCBUFSIZ_LARGE) and pass that size, leaving no room for the terminator. count_lines() in the same file already allocates HCBUFSIZ_LARGE+1. At v7.1.2 the write is src/filehandling.c:1059. Local file input, UI required; ASAN reports WRITE of size 1 / SIGSEGV. CVE-2026-68767 is PUBLISHED (not withdrawn/rejected).

round11_research.bug_semantics: On --restore, hashcat reads argc/argv from a binary restore file and re-parses them with the full option table (user_options_getopt; originally getopt_long) after discarding the user's typed command line. round11_research.bug_semantics: GraphQL-Ruby’s `Schema.max_query_string_tokens` is a parse-time throttle (CWE-770) intended to reject maliciously large query strings. In the default Ruby lexer, `Lexer#advance` skipped `IGNORE_REGEXP`, which treated GraphQL comments (`#...`) as ignorable whitespace, then incremented `@tokens_count` only for the remaining punctuation/name/number/string tokens. An attacker can pad a small executable query with thousands of `# comment N\n` lines so the lexer still scans and allocates over the configured token budget while `@tokens_count` never trips `This query is too large to execute.` GraphQL-CParser is not affected: its ragel lexer `emit()`s COMMENT tokens and increments `tokens_count` before dropping comments from the parser token list. The limit was introduced in v2.3.1 and patched in 2.3.23 / 2.4.18 / 2.5.26 / 2.6.1.
evidence: Advisory GHSA-3h96-34p3-xm76 (cve_id null, withdrawn_at null, identifiers GHSA-only): Ruby lexer does not count comment tokens toward max_query_string_tokens; CParser unaffected; feature introduced v2.3.1; patched 2.3.23 / 2.4.18 / 2.5.26 / 2.6.1. GitHub advisory API and OSV (nvd_published_at null, no CVE alias) match. CVE.org has no CVE record for this GHSA.

round11_research.bug_semantics: CWE-552 information exposure: Tainacan stores item documents under the web-accessible WordPress uploads tree at wp-content/uploads/tainacan-items/{collection_id}/{item_id}/. When an item or collection is not public, only the on-disk folder name is prefixed with the constant _x_ (TAINACAN_PRIVATE_FOLDER_PREFIX); wp_get_attachment_url / image_get_intermediate_size strip that prefix so the published URL looks like a normal uploads path. At 1.0.0, add_htaccess_rules() only wrote Deny from all into uploads/tainacan (logs/csv), not uploads/tainacan-items.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Traefik's Kubernetes CRD provider treats crossProviderNamespaces as an allowlist for which namespaces may emit cross-provider references from IngressRoute, IngressRouteTCP, IngressRouteUDP, and TraefikService. HTTP service serversTransport names containing '@' are rejected unless the parent namespace is on that list (makeServersTransportKey). IngressRouteTCP service serversTransport names go through makeTCPServersTransportKey, which returns a qualified name such as foo@file after only the older AllowCrossNamespace/@kubernetescrd suffix check. A low-privileged CRD author in a namespace omitted from the allowlist can therefore force Traefik to store LoadBalancer.ServersTransport="foo@file" and, at dial time, apply that file-provider TCPServersTransport's mTLS client certificates, SPIFFE identity, or PROXY-protocol settings. CWE-863 incorrect authorization; the HTTP sibling proves the intended gate.

round11_research.bug_semantics: In Traefik's Kubernetes CRD provider, configBuilder.nameAndService (pkg/provider/kubernetes/crd/kubernetes_http.go) is the service-resolver for IngressRoute/TraefikService backendRefs. After the BIC, names without '@' still DeepCopy, fill Namespace from the parent, and reject via isNamespaceAllowed(allowCrossNamespace, parentNs, service.Namespace). Names containing providerNamespaceSeparator ('@') skip that entire branch. The only remaining gate is isCrossProviderNamespaceAllowed(crossProviderNamespaces, parentNs), which returns true when the allowlist is nil (the default). Sibling resolvers (Provider.resolveReference for middlewares/TLS options; makeServersTransportKey for HTTP ServersTransport) already reject strings.HasSuffix(name, '@'+providerName) when allowCrossNamespace is false; nameAndService never did. A tenant confined to namespace attacker can therefore set services: [{name: '<victim-ns>-<svc>@kubernetescrd', kind: TraefikService}]. fullServiceName then splitSvcNameProvider-s the suffix, takes the pName==providerName (kubernetescrd) arm, and returns provider.Normalize(fmt.Sprintf('%s-%s', service.Namespace, name)). Because Namespace was never filled, service.Namespace is empty, so Normalize strips the leading hyphen and yields the victim TraefikService id ('<victim-ns>-<svc>'). The attacker's Host() router is generated bound to that backend despite providers.kubernetesCRD.allowCrossNamespace defaulting to false (Go zero-value bool; no SetDefaults sets it true).

round11_research.flaw_origin: The isolation hole was first written by 36a565a599986afa9e2636d1e3f008c807ee13ec ('Fix cross-provider ref check for Kubernetes CRD provider', 2026-05-07, PR traefik/traefik#13121). Parent 28604083a41b6d6e8c206d71e0bce464bff1edb7 always DeepCopied the LoadBalancerSpec, filled Namespace via namespaceOrParentNamespace, and applied isNamespaceAllowed unconditionally, then called isCrossProviderNamespaceAllowed against service.Namespace. That combination blocked namespace-field cross-ns TraefikService refs and, for '@kubernetescrd' names, prefixed the parent namespace in fullServiceName so 'victim-backend@kubernetescrd' became 'parent-victim-backend' rather than the victim id. The BIC wrapped both the DeepCopy/namespace fill and isNamespaceAllowed inside if !strings.Contains(service.Name, providerNamespaceSeparator), and restricted the crossProviderNamespaces check to '@'-names against parentNamespace. That is the exact skip-@ control flow the advisory describes. The commit did not copy the sibling '!allowCrossNamespace && HasSuffix(@kubernetescrd)' rejection already present in resolveReference and makeServersTransportKey, so '@kubernetescrd' TraefikService refs became an allowCrossNamespace=false bypass. This is not a move/refactor of already-exploitable lines: git log -L :nameAndService first attributes the skip wrapping to this commit, and the parent tree still has the unconditional isNamespaceAllowed. TraefikService resolution itself dates to f30a52c2 (2019) and allowCrossNamespace to 7ba907f2 (2020, default-false since 3072354c in 2021), but those earlier forms did not skip the namespace check/fill for '@' names.

round11_research.bug_semantics: CWE-59 link following in Git LFS working-tree population: git lfs checkout and git lfs pull (and, in 0.5.2–0.5.x, git lfs fetch/get when the fetched ref was HEAD) opened the destination path with Go os.Create, which dereferences a terminal symlink and truncates an existing hard-linked inode. A colliding symlink or hard link at an LFS-tracked path therefore caused LFS object bytes to be written to an attacker-chosen location the user can access, including outside the work tree. A later MkdirAll on the parent path also traversed intermediate directory symlinks, and a bare-repo path-join bug (empty LocalWorkingDir joined with strings.Join, producing /<repo-relative-path> then filepath.Rel) could write outside a bare repository. Git's smudge filter path was not the issue: it writes to stdout and Git creates the file.

round11_research.bug_semantics: DNSIncoming._decode_labels_at_offset recurses once per RFC 1035 §4.1.4 DNS-name compression pointer. Cycle detection (seen_pointers) and MAX_DNS_LABELS=128 capped repeated offsets and label count, but a chain of unique forward pointers that add no extra labels was unbounded. A single ~3 kB mDNS datagram with ~1500 such pointers exceeds CPython's default recursion limit. DECODE_EXCEPTIONS was (IndexError, struct.error, IncomingDecodeError) and omitted RecursionError, so the exception escaped DNSIncoming.__init__ to asyncio's default handler. Any unauthenticated host on the local link (UDP/5353, 224.0.0.251 / ff02::fb) can force sustained CPU burn and log flooding.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Community-tier harden-runner (non-TLS step-security/agent) enforces egress-policy:block with iptables domain allowlisting. addBlockRules always ACCEPTs all TCP to resolver IPs (originally 8.8.8.8, later also 8.8.4.4 and 1.1.1.1) so the agent can resolve names over HTTPS/DoH, with no owner-UID match and no --dport 443 restriction. Enterprise agent-ebpf is unchanged and out of scope. Requires code execution in the job.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated Jolokia exec of BrokerView.addNetworkConnector(String)/addConnector(String) accepts discovery URIs. CVE-2026-34197 added a scheme deny-list (vm, later other transports) in BrokerView.validateAllowedUrl/validateAllowedUri, but nested-component inspection is gated on URISupport.isCompositeURI(), which is true only when the scheme-specific part starts with '('. Discovery wrappers such as static: and masterslave: also accept non-parenthesized forms (static:vm://..., masterslave:vm://...,...); URISupport.parseComposite still splits those into inner URIs. The inner vm://...?brokerConfig=xbean:... therefore skips the deny-list, reaches VMTransportFactory, and loads attacker-controlled Spring XML via ResourceXmlApplicationContext before BrokerService validation, yielding RCE (CWE-20/CWE-94). Patched by always calling parseComposite so missing parentheses are walked the same way transports construct the objects.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Community-tier Harden-Runner (non-TLS `step-security/agent`) enforces `egress-policy: block` with iptables ACCEPT-then-REJECT on OUTPUT/DOCKER-USER. In `addBlockRules`, hardcoded public resolvers (originally 8.8.8.8; later also 8.8.4.4 and 1.1.1.1) were ACCEPTed for all TCP with no `--dport` and no `--uid-owner`. The local DNS proxy listens only on UDP (`127.0.0.1:53` and `172.17.0.1:53`, `Net: "udp"`) and the audit/proxy path drops UDP/53, not TCP/53. A process with workflow code execution can therefore send DNS-over-TCP (`dig +tcp @8.8.8.8`) to those resolvers and get outbound communication that evades `allowed-endpoints`. Enterprise `agent-ebpf` (TLS path) is not this sink.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Traefik Kubernetes Gateway provider option crossProviderNamespaces is documented as allowing only listed Gateway API route namespaces to declare TraefikService backendRefs such as api@internal, dashboard@internal, or rest@internal. For HTTPRoute rules with a single internal backend, the provider correctly checks route.Namespace. For mixed/WRR rules, loadService overwrites namespace from backendRef.Namespace (legitimate for core Service lookup and ReferenceGrant) and then loadHTTPBackendRef runs isCrossProviderNamespaceAllowed against that target namespace. round11_research.bug_semantics: When a broker has a network connector with syncDurableSubs=true, TransportConnection.processBrokerInfo() treats an inbound OpenWire BrokerInfo (networkConnection=true) as a durable-sync request and immediately dispatchSync()s a BrokerSubscriptionInfo that enumerates every durable topic subscription on the broker (copied ConsumerInfo: clientId, subscriptionName, destination, JMS selector). An unauthenticated attacker who can reach the OpenWire port therefore spoofs a network-bridge BrokerInfo and receives the full durable-subscription metadata set.

round11_research.bug_semantics: DNSCache._async_add stored every incoming mDNS response record under the lowercased name in cache, _expirations, _expire_heap, and (for DNSService) service_cache with no entry-count cap. RecordManager.async_updates_from_response feeds every non-expired answer from any UDP/5353 multicast packet (224.0.0.251 / ff02::fb) into that path. An unauthenticated LAN peer can flood unique names (RFC 6762 §11, up to 253 bytes) so the maps grow without bound; the only pre-existing controls were a PTR TTL floor (_DNS_PTR_MIN_TTL=1125s) that actually prolongs attacker records and async_expire every _CACHE_CLEANUP_INTERVAL=10s, which cannot keep up. Unique-name floods OOM memory-constrained consumers; a second variant replays cached records with shifting TTLs so _expire_heap grows between cleanups without changing cache/_total_records.

round11_research.bug_semantics: When providers.kubernetesCRD.allowCrossNamespace=false, Traefik rejects direct IngressRoute middleware refs that name another namespace, but createChainMiddleware still honors MiddlewareRef.namespace on spec.chain.middlewares[] and emits makeID(foreignNS, name) with no isNamespaceAllowed check. A principal who can write a local Chain CRD can therefore bind and apply another namespace's middleware (stripPrefix, headers, forwardAuth, etc.) onto routes in their own namespace, bypassing the documented CRD isolation boundary.

round11_research.bug_semantics: RabbitTemplate.sendAndReceive() with a configured fixed reply queue correlates replies by a messageTag written into the AMQP correlationId (or a custom correlation header). That tag was generated from a per-instance AtomicInteger (messageTagProvider.incrementAndGet()), producing sequential, guessable identifiers that restart at 1 on each new RabbitTemplate. Two templates sharing one reply queue therefore overlap in identifier space; an actor who can publish to that queue can inject a forged reply or steal a legitimate one before the real response arrives (CWE-330 reply poisoning). The same counter also tagged the temporary-queue path; the CVE attack is the shared fixed-queue case. userCorrelationId only opts out when the caller already supplied a unique id.

round11_research.bug_semantics: netty_unix_socket_recvFd (JNI, used by Epoll/KQueue DomainSocketChannel in DomainSocketReadMode.FILE_DESCRIPTORS) allocates a control buffer of CMSG_SPACE(sizeof(int)) — 24 bytes on 64-bit Linux — and accepts an SCM_RIGHTS cmsg only when cmsg_len == CMSG_LEN(sizeof(int)) (20). A peer can send two fds in one cmsg (cmsg_len = CMSG_LEN(8) = 24). That payload fits the buffer exactly, so the kernel installs both descriptors with no MSG_CTRUNC. The equality check then fails, the accept/close branch is skipped, and neither installed fd is closed. The native for(;;) retries recvmsg; on a non-blocking socket the retry returns EAGAIN, Java maps that to 0, and the Java read loop exits normally. Two fds leak per crafted message. There is no MSG_CTRUNC handling and extra SCM_RIGHTS fds are never closed.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated Jolokia/JMX callers of DestinationView.sendTextMessage* build a VM transport URL by concatenating "vm://" with ManagedRegionBroker.getBrokerName(). A malicious broker name that includes a query such as "?brokerConfig=xbean:http://attacker/poc.xml" (RegionBroker.setBrokerName was public and unvalidated, bypassing BrokerService's illegal-character rewrite) makes VMTransportFactory treat the host as a missing broker and load attacker-controlled Spring XML through XBeanBrokerFactory. ResourceXmlApplicationContext instantiates singleton beans before BrokerService validates the configuration, so factory methods such as Runtime.exec() run in the broker JVM.

round11_research.bug_semantics: The timestamp-authority HTTP server installs wrapMetrics inside setupGlobalMiddleware, which the source comments as running before routing. wrapMetrics records Prometheus histogram/summary/counter vectors using the raw request path (r.URL.Path) and, after later monitoring additions, the raw HTTP method (r.Method) as label values. client_golang registers a permanent time series for every distinct label set, so an unauthenticated client can send unique unmatched paths (for example /api/v1/timestamp/<uuid>) or arbitrary methods, including those that 404, and grow unbounded in-process metric cardinality until the process OOMs (CWE-770).

round11_research.bug_semantics: Cargo CanonicalUrl always chopped a trailing .git from registry index URLs. That is correct for git indexes, where host/index and host/index.git are the same repository, but wrong for sparse indexes, which are ordinary HTTPS paths and treat those URLs as distinct registries. SourceId equality and hashing use kind plus CanonicalUrl, so sparse+https://host/index and sparse+https://host/index.git intern as the same identity and share the configured Cargo token. An attacker who can publish on a sparse registry that allows cross-registry dependencies and who can host a sibling *.git sparse index requiring auth can publish a crate depending on the sibling; when the victim fetches it, Cargo sends the victim's token to the malicious index.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Netty's HAProxy PROXY protocol v2 decoder recursively parses nested PP2_TYPE_SSL TLVs, each as a retainedSlice of the channel cumulation buffer. readTlvs() flattens only the immediate children of top-level SSL TLVs into HAProxyMessage.tlvs(); depth-2+ encapsulated TLVs stay solely on HAProxySSLTLV.encapsulatedTLVs(). HAProxySSLTLV does not override deallocate, and HAProxyMessage.deallocate() only walks the flattened list, so a syntactically valid nested-SSL header parses, fires downstream, and is released by the application while the depth-2+ slices permanently pin the pooled ByteBuf (CWE-401).
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-48059 (CNA GitHub, updated 2026-06-12) describes nested PP2_TYPE_SSL TLV memory leak prior to 4.1.135.Final and 4.2.15.Final; GHSA-h2qv-fj59-j46j withdrawn_at=null, github_reviewed, CVSS 7.5 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H. Not withdrawn/rejected.

round11_research.bug_semantics: XORMappedAddress.GetFromAs decodes the STUN address family with bin.Uint16(value[0:2]) before checking that the XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS attribute value is long enough. Message.Decode stores attr.Value as a subslice of the remaining buffer (b[:aL]); STUN pads lengths 1–3 to 4 bytes, but a 0-length value has no padding. When that 0-length attribute is last in a tightly allocated Raw buffer (cap==len), the value slice has cap 0, so value[0:2] is a runtime slice-bounds panic. A remote Binding-success (or any parsed STUN/ICE message) carrying a trailing 0-length XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS therefore DoSes the process (CWE-20). The later len(value)<=4 check sat after the family read and could not prevent this panic.

round11_research.bug_semantics: CodeIgniter 4 file-upload rules is_image and mime_in classify an upload solely by content-derived MIME type and never independently enforce that a non-empty client filename extension is a safe image/matching type. is_image maps UploadedFile::getExtension() (MIME-guessed, not the client name) through Mimes::guessTypeFromExtension() and accepts the file if that type starts with 'image'. mime_in compares UploadedFile::getMimeType()/getType() (finfo of the temp file) against the allowed list. An attacker can prepend image magic bytes (for example GIF89a) to a PHP webshell named shell.php; both rules pass, and if the application then saves the upload with the client-supplied name into a web-accessible script-enabled directory, the file is executed as PHP (CWE-434). The attack requires all three of: is_image/mime_in used without a separate safe-extension check (ext_in on patched versions), preservation of the original filename, and a public executable upload path.

Host-only keys used exact equality and were not this bug; the integrity issue is the host+path substring match on request metadata.

round11_research.bug_semantics: CWE-601 open redirect (and cache-poisoning amplifier) in @angular/ssr: an unsanitized X-Forwarded-Prefix is passed into joinUrlParts() and then addLeadingSlash() when emitting a redirect Location. addLeadingSlash only treats a leading '/' as already-absolute, so a prefix of '\evil.com' becomes '/\evil.com'. Browsers treat the '/\' sequence as a protocol-relative '//', sending the client to the attacker host. After CVE-2026-27738, INVALID_PREFIX_REGEX /^[/\\]{2}/ rejected two leading slash-or-backslash characters (//, \\, /\, \\/) but still accepted a single leading backslash; the same prepend-slash transform therefore remained exploitable. Redirects also omitted Vary: X-Forwarded-Prefix, so a poisoned Location could be cached.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-33397 state=PUBLISHED (cvelistV5 2026-03-30, not rejected); GHSA-vfx2-hv2g-xj5f withdrawn_at=null; NVD/OSV alias the same GHSA. Real incomplete-fix open redirect of CVE-2026-27738, not a false positive.

Attack: AngularServerApp.handle() uses joinUrlParts(X-Forwarded-Prefix, redirect path) as Location. Prefix '\evil.com' + '/home' => '/\evil.com/home'. Browsers interpret '/\' as '//'.

round11_research.bug_semantics: FileBinding.write and ZipFileBinding.write join a FileCredentials-supplied name onto a per-build secrets directory with FilePath.child and then copyFrom/unzipFrom that path. FilePath.child honors ../ and path separators, so a credential whose getFileName() is a traversal payload (e.g. ../../../../p0wn3d.txt, as in Security3672Test) writes the secret bytes (or extracts a zip) outside the intended UUID secrets dir on the node filesystem. If a low-privileged user can supply file/zip credentials used by a job on the built-in node, the write can land under JENKINS_HOME (init.groovy.d, plugins) and become RCE. FileCredentials javadoc claimed a simple basename, but the binding never enforced that contract; FileCredentialsImpl UI upload strips prefixes, yet programmatic/XML constructors and other implementations can return unsanitized names.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-42520 state=PUBLISHED (cveMetadata.datePublished=2026-04-29, dateUpdated=2026-04-29); CNA Jenkins; affected Credentials Binding Plugin 0 through 719.v80e905ef14eb_; not rejected/withdrawn. GHSA-p2rf-wpxj-mx2g withdrawn_at=null.

round11_research.bug_semantics: free5GC NEF treats an outbound PFD-subscription notification failure as process-fatal. PfdChangeNotifier.FlushNotifications() asynchronously POSTs a PfdChangeNotification to the stored subscriber notifyUri; on any client error (connection refused, DNS failure, TLS error, timeout) it calls logger.PFDManageLog.Fatal(err). PFDManageLog is a logrus.Entry, so Fatal is os.Exit(1)-equivalent: it bypasses Gin recovery, deferred cleanup, and connection draining and terminates the entire NEF process. An attacker who can create a PFD subscription with an unreachable notifyUri and then trigger a PFD change (AF traffic-influence + PFD subscription + PFD transaction) gets a deterministic NEF crash. The PFD transaction itself returns 201; the exit happens on the async notify. In v4.2.1 the trigger chain is unauthenticated because the NEF SBI route groups lack inbound auth (tracked separately in free5gc#858/#859/#862); this case is the Fatal-on-delivery-failure defect (CWE-617/CWE-755/CWE-20).

round11_research.bug_semantics: Composer Perforce::generateP4Command() built a single shell string by concatenating the p4 executable with unescaped -u (user), -c (client), and -p (port) values, then ProcessExecutor::execute() ran that string via the shell. A malicious root composer.json (or composer config) declaring a type=perforce VCS repository could put shell metacharacters in repositories[].url (copied to VcsDriver::$url and Perforce::$p4Port), repositories[].p4user, and the depot-derived client name. PerforceDriver::initialize() calls p4Login()/isLoggedIn()/connectClient(), so generateP4Command() runs during ordinary Composer use of that project. A payload such as url=localhost:1666; touch /tmp/pwned becomes `p4 -u … -p localhost:1666; touch /tmp/pwned …`; the shell still executes the injected command if p4 is missing. Dependency composer.json files are not a vector. Distinct from GHSA-gqw4-4w2p-838q (unescaped $sourceReference on sync) and from later rsh:/jsh: P4PORT transport execution.

round11_research.bug_semantics: NEF mounted the AF-facing /3gpp-traffic-influence/v1 CRUD routes without inbound bearer-token authentication or authorization. Requests with no Authorization header or a forged token reached handlers that create, read, patch, and delete traffic-influence subscriptions; the route group was mounted regardless of ServiceList, so disabling the service in configuration did not remove exposure.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Netmaker exposed an HTTP handler that terminates the server process with syscall.Kill(Getpid(), SIGINT). As shipped this was POST /api/server/shutdown in controllers/server.go serverHandlers, registered with no Authorize, allowUsers, or logic.SecurityCheck wrapper while neighboring /api/server routes used those wrappers. HttpMiddlewares carried no authentication (only an optional Pro unlicensed-API gate), so any network client could POST the endpoint and interrupt the process. With a restart supervisor this produced cyclic denial of service at roughly 3-second intervals. CVE-2026-29771 / GHSA-rhr9-hgcm-x289 (CWE-404); CVSS 4.0 PR:N matches the unauthenticated registration. The first code-level patch wrapped the handler in logic.SecurityCheck(true).

round11_research.bug_semantics: The Vision Chat paste-image handler derives the uploaded PNG filename from MD5(PIL.Image.tobytes()). PIL tobytes() serializes pixel or palette-index bytes but omits image dimensions, mode, palette, and transparency metadata, so visually different palette images can share the same digest and filename. In a shared instance, a second upload can overwrite the first file, and the vision model later fetches attacker-controlled content through the unchanged file URL.

round11_research.bug_semantics: A routing message can select a definition that composes the routing function with itself. The catalog returns a composed FunctionInvocationWrapper whose target is a composition lambda, so RoutingFunction's direct-target self check does not recognize it as the router; applying the wrapper invokes the router again on the same input, producing unbounded recursion and eventual OOM denial of service.

round11_research.bug_semantics: xmldom's SAX parser can accept a deeply nested XML document, but seven subsequent DOM operations traversed that tree with unbounded JavaScript recursion. round11_research.bug_semantics: A malicious Composer repository can put shell metacharacters after the @ delimiter in a package's Perforce source reference. round11_research.bug_semantics: Attacker-controlled input reaches IOFactory::load(), which calls createReaderForFile() and File::assertFile(). File::prohibitWrappers() tried to reject stream wrappers by accepting parse_url($filename, PHP_URL_SCHEME) only when it returned a string longer than one character. For a valid PHP stream path such as phar:///path/file.phar/inner, parse_url returns false, so the guard is skipped while PHP still opens the phar wrapper. round11_research.bug_semantics: RabbitConnectionFactoryBean.setUri() immediately delegated an amqps URI to the RabbitMQ client while the bean's secure setUpSSL() path remained conditional on a separate useSSL flag. With the default false flag, the client created encrypted TLS using its permissive trust-everything setup, so neither the broker certificate nor hostname was verified and an active network attacker could impersonate the broker.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Vert.x's RFC 3986 dot-segment remover mishandled rule C when processing /../ or terminal /.. after an output segment containing no slash: the pos != -1 guard left that whole segment in the output instead of clearing it. Consequently a decoded path such as bar/../index.html normalized to bar/index.html rather than /index.html; a crafted static-handler request containing bar%2F..%2F could resolve a nonexistent offset and cache that negative result so later requests for the real static file returned HTTP 404, causing unauthenticated availability loss.
evidence: The Eclipse CNA record https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-1002 is PUBLISHED and describes network-triggered static-handler cache manipulation and availability loss; it marks Vert.x 4.0.0 through 4.5.23 and 5.0.0 through 5.0.6 affected.

Vendor issue https://github.com/vert-x3/vertx-web/issues/2836 demonstrates removeDotSegments("bar/../index.html") returning "bar/index.html" instead of "/index.html" and records that a bar%2F..%2F request caches a nonexistent file result, after which the normal file request returns 404.

round11_research.bug_semantics: In devalue.parse/unflatten, typed-array records recursively hydrated the attacker-selected value[1] and passed the result directly to a typed-array constructor without verifying that it was an ArrayBuffer.
