round11_research.bug_semantics: A malicious .crate tarball served by a third-party registry can place a symlink under its own <crate>-<version> cache directory and then place a later entry whose syntactically valid in-crate path traverses that symlink. Cargo extracts registry crates beneath one shared registry source directory, so following the symlink can write one level below the malicious crate's directory and replace files in a sibling crate cache; a later build then compiles the attacker's replacement source. crates.io's upload policy rejects symlinks, but third-party registries need not do so.
evidence: The Rust Security Response Team advisory https://blog.rust-lang.org/2026/05/25/cve-2026-5223/ states that a crafted third-party-registry tarball can extract one level below its own cache directory and overwrite another crate's cached source; crates.io is not affected because it forbids symlinks; all Cargo versions shipped before Rust 1.96.0 are affected.

The authoritative CVE.org record returned by https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-5223 is PUBLISHED, identifies Rust Project Cargo versions >=1.0.0 and <1.96.0 as affected, and names Rust 1.96.0's rejection of all tar symlinks as the solution; there is no rejected or withdrawn vendor disposition.

round11_research.bug_semantics: Schema.load(data, many=True) records validation failures by index. For each new invalid item, ErrorStore.store_error wrapped the message as {index: messages} and called merge_errors on the entire accumulated self.errors dictionary; merge_errors copied that growing dictionary before adding the new key. A request with n invalid items therefore copied 0+1+...+(n-1) prior entries, producing quadratic CPU work and disproportionate denial-of-service amplification.

round11_research.bug_semantics: With RBAC enabled, check_rbac() matched role-restricted paths against the raw, percent-encoded ngx.var.request_uri using ngx.re.find(). Nginx selected its serving location from a decoded and normalized URI, so an authenticated low-privilege request such as /%68tadmin.php could reach the htadmin location while the Lua pattern missed; the unmatched-path branch then returned ngx.HTTP_OK.
evidence: CVE.org record CVE-2026-19670 is PUBLISHED and describes the raw percent-encoded request URI versus nginx decoded-location mismatch; it marks Malcolm versions through 26.07.1 affected and states that 26.08.0 addresses the issue.
git show eb4e64da6da1ee764d0ac9c83e1f0a9280003211 shows check_rbac() changing exactly from 'local uri = ngx.var.uri' to 'local uri = ngx.var.request_uri:match("^[^?]+") or ""'.
git show e87c50c30d60551185305e2d045c11c3509dbda0:nginx/lua/nginx_auth_helpers.lua confirms the parent used ngx.var.uri before matching path_role_envs and returned ngx.HTTP_OK when no rule matched.

git show 82b5fc5271fe6844520afca6ef68cf615b67113f adds ngx.unescape_uri(path) before slash/traversal normalization and lowercasing; its parent 538057a7c0776010efe40aa71874db06f1c7d42d still passed the raw request URI through normalization without percent-decoding.

git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms the introducer is an ancestor of the direct fix. Tag containment shows v26.07.1 contains the introducer but not the fix, while v26.08.0 contains the fix, matching the CVE release boundary.
git cat-file -p eb4e64da6da1ee764d0ac9c83e1f0a9280003211 shows one parent, a Seth Grover author/committer identity, a PGP signature, and no AI-related message or trailer.
round11_research.flaw_origin: Commit eb4e64da6da1ee764d0ac9c83e1f0a9280003211 introduced the percent-encoding mismatch by replacing ngx.var.uri with ngx.var.request_uri:match("^[^?]+") in check_rbac(). Its immediate parent e87c50c30d60551185305e2d045c11c3509dbda0 used ngx.var.uri, so the raw-URI source did not exist there. The commit is a one-parent, two-line change rather than a merge, move, revert, or squash aggregate.
round11_research.reasoning: The advisory's vulnerable source-to-sink path is present in the clone: raw request_uri enters check_rbac(), path_role_envs is matched with ngx.re.find(), and a percent-encoded miss reaches the fail-open HTTP_OK branch. The smallest public commit that first writes the decisive raw-URI source is eb4e64da6da1ee764d0ac9c83e1f0a9280003211; its parent uses nginx's normalized ngx.var.uri. Commit 82b5fc5271fe6844520afca6ef68cf615b67113f directly closes it with ngx.unescape_uri and is included in the stated fixed release. Because the BIC itself has no AI marker and is signed under a human author/committer identity, this real vulnerability is classified NOT_AI.

round11_research.bug_semantics: In the public photo image view, an unauthenticated request-controlled order value other than created reaches DBStructure::existsColumn('photo', [$order_field]). existsColumn concatenates that value inside SHOW COLUMNS FROM `photo` LIKE '<value>' and calls DBA::p with no bound arguments; DBA::p consequently uses PDO::query or mysqli::query. A quote-bearing order value can therefore alter the SQL statement before the value is later accepted as an ORDER BY field.
evidence: The frozen bundle and live GitHub advisory identify GHSA-8xqr-cc5h-9wvp / CVE-2026-72550 as an unauthenticated SQL injection through the photo-view order parameter; CVE.org state is PUBLISHED and lists versions through 2026.08-dev as affected.
At origin/develop mod/photos.php, the view path assigns $_GET['order'] to $order_field and sends any nonempty non-created value to DBStructure::existsColumn('photo', [$order_field]).

At origin/develop src/Database/DBStructure.php, existsColumn forms SHOW COLUMNS FROM the escaped table name but directly concatenates the unescaped column between single quotes, then calls DBA::p($sql).
At origin/develop src/Database/Database.php, p() uses PDO::query when there are no arguments and mysqli::query for SHOW statements/no arguments, establishing the raw query sink.

git log -S for DBStructure::existsColumn('photo' isolates f8f3689a0d7fa0c2ed886646dde8d284233e923f; its patch adds the import and the existsColumn predicate only, and its sole parent is fde223327fb39b0dff84eceb2af29734f7c78aac.
The parent version at fde223327fb39b0dff84eceb2af29734f7c78aac has only elseif (!empty($order_field)) and therefore lacks the vulnerable existsColumn source-to-sink edge.
The BIC is contained by release tag 2023.04 and every later local release tag through 2026.05-1, as well as origin/stable, origin/develop, and origin/2026.08-rc.
The dangerous caller and sink remain present in origin/stable, origin/develop, and origin/2026.08-rc after the advisory publication date; no direct fix is present in the available clone refs.

The BIC's full local commit object and GitHub commit API response contain no AI attribution, assistant trailer, generated-by marker, or bot identity; the API reports a verified PGP signature for the matching human author and committer.

Its direct parent passed the value only to the structured select order option and did not connect it to existsColumn's raw SHOW COLUMNS construction, so this one-parent, three-line commit is the smallest public object that created the advisory's source-to-sink path.

The atomic causal change is f8f3689a0d7fa0c2ed886646dde8d284233e923f, not the older existsColumn implementation by itself, because the direct parent has no untrusted call edge to that sink. potential_fix.approach: Stop interpolating $column in DBStructure::existsColumn: bind the LIKE value as a query parameter; if SHOW COLUMNS cannot be prepared on a supported driver, validate the requested column against the static photo schema before calling existsColumn.
potential_fix.rationale: This removes request data from raw SQL at the shared sink while preserving the intended dynamic sort-field check; a static schema allowlist is the safe fallback for drivers that cannot prepare SHOW statements.
